entry.title: South Florida families turn to resale shopping to save money as holiday season approaches
entry.summary: Shoppers were out at the South Florida Fairgrounds on Friday looking for bargains at a large resale event featuring children's items. 'I love the fact that I can save a lot of money, and I like the shopping experience,' said Tatiana, a shopper who drove from Port St. Lucie. WATCH REPORT BELOW: South Florida families turn to resale shopping to save The resale event is run by Just Between Friends Palm Beach, a consignment shop. Among the items for sale were tables of toys, racks of clothing and various accessories from playpens to bicycles and strollers. 'Everything here is brought in by local families that have gently used items that their kids have outgrown, and instead of throwing it away, they're able to come bring it here and help other families save on items,' says store owner Kim Hazim. Resale shops are growing in popularity as inflation strains family budgets, and Hazim said this event has grown over the years. 'We used to be in 15,000 square feet; now we're in 30,000 square feet because that's how many families really need to come out,' Hazim said. Many were getting an early jump on holiday shopping with Black Friday coming later this month, but deals are already out there. 'Black Friday is almost a month-long event,' says money-saving expert Andrea Woroch. 'Retailers like Best Buy, Nordstrom, even Sephora, they started rolling out doorbuster-like deals on Nov. 1.' She added that good deals are already out there. 'If you're seeing a good deal, and again, I think that 30% off benchmark is a great place to make a purchase at,' Woroch said. 'And keep in mind, some retailers will offer price adjustments within a week or two weeks.'

entry.title: Russian national pleads guilty in $7 million Palm Beach County Medicare fraud, laundering scheme
entry.summary: A Russian national pleaded guilty Friday to his role in a Medicare fraud scheme rooted in Palm Beach County, marking the first conviction in a case I first brought to you last year. In federal court, 29-year-old Nika Machutadze, with the help of a translator, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering. He is one of the defendants linked to a fraudulent medical equipment company in Delray Beach called Sunshine Senior Solutions , and he admitted under oath to his involvement in a money laundering scheme totaling more than $7 million. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Russian national pleads guilty in $7 million Palm Beach County Medicare fraud Machutadze could face up to 20 years in prison, plus fines, restitution and deportation. Seniors first contacted me last year, sharing Medicare statements for medical equipment they didn't need or receive from Sunshine Senior Solutions. While I tallied up hundreds of thousands of dollars in false claims from the statements I reviewed, that was a drop in the bucket, according to federal prosecutors. Federal prosecutors say Sunshine Senior Solutions billed insurers for more than $3 billion, though only a fraction of that was paid out. Machutadze admitted to opening bank accounts for Sunshine Senior Solutions and a second similar business in Texas, and transferring some of the money paid by insurers overseas. I reached out to some of the seniors to share the news of the guilty plea. 'Oh, that's terrific,' said Laura Carmine, of Illinois. 'Nice to know that justice can be done.' 'I'm glad to hear that,' said Mike Parrett, of Ohio. I spoke with Machutadze's attorney, Tony Mirvis, after Friday's hearing. 'The government's evidence was overwhelming,' Mirvis said. Mirvis said his client thought he was just taking a job. 'What I think is important is he's like the tip of the spear,' Mirvis said. 'I hate to say it, but he's kind of like a victim because the people that got him to work they're the ones that are making the millions of dollars, and he's making like literally nothing. Hilmi, who is also tied to Sunshine Senior Solutions, is scheduled for trial in February. entry.title: Democrat Eileen Laubacher flips Colorado House seat, ousting Lauren Boebert
entry.summary: Democrat Eileen Laubacher has defeated Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert in Colorado's 4th Congressional District, according to a race call by The Associated Press more than a week after Election Day. The race remained too close to call for days as election officials continued counting ballots. Laubacher's victory unseats one of President Donald Trump's most outspoken allies in Congress. Boebert has represented Colorado's 4th Congressional District since 2025. She previously represented the state's 3rd Congressional District but switched districts in late 2023, citing the need for a 'fresh start following a difficult year' that included family turmoil and several controversies. Laubacher, a retired Navy admiral who served in the military for more than 30 years, said her decision to run for Congress was driven by concerns about the country's future. 'I have never felt as much of a threat to our country, our Constitution, our very democracy, as I do at this time,' Laubacher said.

entry.article_text: Lucie County Sheriff’s Office is seeking help in finding a man accused of stealing from a corner store in the middle of the night. 11, at around 3:45 a.m., an unidentified man entered the MLK Food Corner Store located at 1107 S. 33rd Street, stole $278 in cash from the register while also filing a bag with smoking-related merchandise. The man fled the store on foot after robbing it, and was last seen traveling eastbound on Kentucky Avenue, according to SLCSO . See also: Outlook working again? Why some emails may still be missing after massive Microsoft outage The Sheriff’s Office reports that the burglary resulted in approximately $3,200 in stolen cash and merchandise. Anyone who recognizes the suspect or has information regarding this incident is encouraged to contact the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office at 772-462-7300 or submit a tip to Patroltips@stluciesheriff.com .

entry.summary: Florida’s Turnpike shut down in Martin County after tractor-trailer and pickup crash near Palm City    WPBF
entry.article_text: All northbound lanes were closed on Florida’s Turnpike in Martin County for an hour following a crash involving a tractor-trailer and a pickup truck. Martin County Fire Rescue states the crash happened just before 11 a.m. on Friday near the 137 mile-marker in Palm City. Two drivers involved are said to be safe with no reported injuries, but the Martin County Sheriff's Office said there were minor injuries and significant damage to both vehicles. Martin County Fire Rescue, the Martin County Sheriff’s Office, and the Florida Highway Patrol worked together to clear the debris. The closure caused a backup of nearly 10-mile on the Turnpike. All lanes have since reopened. Follow: Interactive traffic map This is a developing story and will be updated as information becomes available. entry.summary: Florida’s Turnpike closed in both directions in Martin County; truck jackknifed    WPEC
entry.article_text: A crash involving a tractor-trailer and a pickup truck closed all northbound lanes of Florida’s Turnpike near Mile Marker 137 in Palm City on Friday, according to Martin County Fire Rescue. Both drivers were safe, and no injuries were reported. Fire rescue, the Martin County Sheriff’s Office and Florida Highway Patrol were working to clear debris from the roadway. The crash happened just before 11 a.m. Northbound traffic was closed from before Exit 133 for Stuart and Martin Downs Boulevard (State Road 714) to before Mile Marker 137. A separate police activity closure extended from before Mile Marker 130 to Exit 133, and the northbound on-ramp was also closed. Southbound, a jackknifed truck was causing congestion from before Mile Marker 139 to before Mile Marker 137, according to Florida 511. Drivers were advised to take alternate routes and expect delays. entry.title: Delays, cancellations mount at President Donald J. Trump International Airport amid nationwide ground stop
entry.summary: A nationwide ground stop prompted by air traffic control communications issues caused widespread flight disruptions Friday, with passengers across South Florida facing delays and cancellations. The Federal Aviation Administration issued the ground stop as officials investigated the communications problems affecting air traffic control. At President Donald J. Trump International Airport, departure boards showed numerous delays, with some flights being canceled as the disruption continued. One traveler told WPTV reporter Michael Hoffman that she and her husband had planned to fly to Atlanta for a weekend trip but were told they likely would not be leaving Friday night. 'They said it didn't look good,' she said, describing what her husband had been told by TSA. 'Probably not leaving tonight.' Although disappointed, she said their travel wasn't urgent. 'This (travel to Atlanta) was just for fun, so disappointing,' she said. 'You know, rather safe than sorry.' Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said officials had no indication at the time that a malicious act or hacking contributed to the communications issues. The FAA remained in the early stages of investigating the problem, and additional information about what caused the disruption and what was being done to resolve it was not immediately available.

entry.title: Harry's Banana Farm owner Harry Seifert Jr. dies at 76, leaving legacy in Lake Worth Beach

There's the raptor on the roof, the colorful atmosphere and the roadside billboard known for its witty, sometimes controversial messages. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Harrys Banana Farm owner dies, leaving legacy of giving 'It's iconic; everybody here knows about the place,' said Vinnie Fiermonte, who lives in Lake Worth Beach. 'A lot of people I know here from Boynton come to Harry's.' Tyler Hart, a local who has visited Harry's Banana Farm, said the bar's unusual personality makes it stand out. 'Definitely the raptor on the roof stands out,' Hart said, adding there are 'always interesting signs on the billboard.' But this week, that billboard is empty as the neighborhood bar mourns the death of its owner, Harry Seifert Jr. Harry died Tuesday from health complications at 76 years old, according to the bar's general manager and Harry's longtime friend, Lou DeStout. DeStout said Harry had survived two strokes over the years and dealt with a number of other health problems. The loss is personal for DeStout, who met Harry in the late 1970s. Their friendship would eventually span decades, other business ventures and Harry's Banana Farm itself. Harry Jr. took over in the early 1980s and helped transform it from a more family-oriented establishment into a late-night hangout. Their friendship would eventually span decades, other business ventures and Harry's Banana Farm itself."Oh, Harry and I met in the late 70s and, uh, we did a lot, we just hit it off instantly," DeStout said. "And he was a larger-than-life character. The whole place is him," DeStout said."He's the one that decorated all the stuff," he added.DeStout said many of the items inside the bar were collected during Harry's travels, with pieces from places including Australia and China.Inside, the bar's walls are a collage of Harry's travels and adventures with treasures at every inch.Harry was also behind another unmistakable piece of the bar's personality: its roadside sign."He was the original sign guy," DeStout said. "Yeah, way back when he started a tradition."DeStout eventually took over the tradition of putting messages on the sign and said he shared Harry's sense of humor."He always enjoyed it too," DeStout said. "But like I said, he was the original guy who did the sign."Harry's health began declining years ago. DeStout said Harry suffered a stroke roughly 17 years ago that paralyzed one side of his body. He recovered before suffering another stroke that took away his voice."He's had numerous other medical problems over the years, and then he started having heart problems and things like that," DeStout said. "So it's, it's been a difficult bunch of years for him."Still, DeStout said Harry continued living his life, traveling and attending events despite those challenges."He still lived life, and he got around more than I did," DeStout said. "He'd go to Las Vegas to the Sphere and the Kravis Center to plays, and, he got out and about a lot more than I did."Since Harry's death, DeStout said he's repeatedly heard one question from customers and employees: What happens to Harry's Banana Farm now?His answer is simple."Nothing. We're gonna continue on like we always do," DeStout said. "I've had to answer that question 100 times in the last two days. It's gonna keep on being Harry's Banana Farm."DeStout said that longevity is notable as Lake Worth Beach and the surrounding area continue to change. He recalled a time when Harry's was one of several similar neighborhood bars along Dixie Highway."When Harry and I tended bar here together 40 years ago, there was 10 places like Harry's up and down Dixie, and they're all gone," DeStout said. "Harry's is the only one that survives, and not only survives but thrives."For the people closest to Harry, his legacy extends beyond the walls of his neighborhood bar.DeStout said roughly 30 years ago, Harry began dressing as Santa Claus and visiting Barton Elementary School to give wrapped gifts to underprivileged children."He started going to Barton Elementary School and handing out wrapped gifts to all the little kids, underprivileged kids," DeStout said.What started at one school grew to include four elementary schools and eventually became a nonprofit, Harry's Helping Hands."And I just thought when we had the idea of making a legitimate nonprofit, it'd be a great legacy to leave behind," DeStout said. And now, after 30 years, it's gangbusters."The effort is marking its 30th year of giving back to the Lake Worth Beach community."He'd be here for the Christmas party; he'd be proud of everybody here for everything that they've done," DeStout said. "We've come so far, for a little neighborhood bar, we've done quite an impact."For DeStout, giving back is part of the responsibility that comes with operating a successful community business."And I believe, you know, very strongly that when, when you do business in the community, you profit from the community, you have a responsibility and obligation to contribute to that community, you know, so that's, and that was always Harry," DeStout said. "Harry was just so generous."DeStout is now encouraging people who want to honor Harry to donate to Harry's Helping Hands in lieu of flowers."He would much prefer a donation because that goes directly to the kids," DeStout said.Customers have also been stopping by Harry's Banana Farm to remember the man behind the business."He was very sarcastic, funny. He not only gave back, but he was a contributor, an active contributor," said Billy Miller, a patron at Harry's Banana Farm. "I would say he's going to be missed, absolutely."Hart shared a similar sentiment."It's definitely a bummer any time you hear a local person like that passes away, hopefully they're able to keep things going," Hart said.Everything DeStout says suggests that is exactly what they intend to do."This whole place is his legacy," DeStout said.And when Lopez asked what he would say to his longtime friend now, DeStout's answer brought that legacy back to where it started."I'll miss you, pal, but we're just gonna keep rolling along, just like we always have," DeStout said.A celebration of life for Harry Seifert Jr. 6 at the Lake Worth Beach Golf Club.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Machutadze admitted to opening bank accounts for Sunshine Senior Solutions and a second similar business in Texas, and transferring some of the money paid by insurers overseas.I reached out to some of the seniors to share the news of the guilty plea."Oh, that's terrific," said Laura Carmine, of Illinois. "Nice to know that justice can be done.""I'm glad to hear that," said Mike Parrett, of Ohio.I spoke with Machutadze's attorney, Tony Mirvis, after Friday's hearing."The government's evidence was overwhelming," Mirvis said. Mirvis said his client thought he was just taking a job."What I think is important is he's like the tip of the spear," Mirvis said. "I hate to say it, but he's kind of like a victim because the people that got him to work— they're the ones that are making the millions of dollars, and he's making like literally nothing. He's getting in trouble for it."Information filed in Friday's case mentions another defendant, Ibrahim Hilmi, and a second, unnamed co-conspirator. Hilmi, who is also tied to Sunshine Senior Solutions, is scheduled for trial in February."Everybody that's involved with this should get prosecuted, and they should get punished for what they did," Mirvis said.Mirvis told me his client will not be cooperating with federal investigators on any other prosecutions.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Martin County firefighters express concerns over staffing levels at Fire Rescue - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County firefighters express concerns over staffing levels at Fire Rescue    WPBF
entry.article_text: A day after the firefighters' union in Martin County expressed concerns about staffing, the County Administrator is responding by acknowledging the concerns while also saying there's not much that can be done right now. The union raised its concerns in a Thursday social media post, pointing out that the county had canceled an upcoming hiring class of 25 new firefighters even as Fire Rescue is understaffed. "It is about public safety, firefighter working conditions, and ensuring Martin County residents receive the level of emergency services they pay for and deserve," the post said. Don Donaldson, the county administrator for Martin County, acknowledged the union's concerns. "I think the concern of the public is real and legitimate," Donaldson said. Donaldson confirmed that fire rescue is already short-staffed by 17 firefighters and that the hiring class will not proceed as planned. However, he clarified that the class is postponed, not canceled. "I don't want to have to lay somebody off six months right after I hire them," Donaldson said. He explained that the delay is due to uncertainties in the county budget caused by Amendment 3, a measure recently approved by Florida voters that will lower property taxes statewide. Martin County estimates the amendment will result in a $75 million revenue loss over the next two years. Donaldson emphasized the need to assess the budget before committing to new hires. "What I didn't want to have happen is to fully fund all of our firefighters and then find we have to eliminate a position or two with somebody already in the position," Donaldson said. Donaldson said he hopes to have more clarification on the hiring of firefighters within the next few months. The agency later lifted the ground stop Friday night, though flight disruptions continued. entry.title: Jupiter’s Feast of Little Italy turns 25 with food, music and cheesy record attempt
entry.summary: Italian food, live music and family traditions return to Abacoa Town Center this weekend as the Galbani Feast of Little Italy celebrates its 25th anniversary Nov. 6-8 with three days of festivities and free admission, according to organizers. The festival runs from 4 to 10 p.m. Friday, 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. Saturday and 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Sunday. This year's milestone celebration includes Italian food, cooking demonstrations, live entertainment, family activities and an unusual attempt to make festival history using string cheese. Italian favorites fill Abacoa Food is at the heart of the weekend. Festival organizers say guests can expect Italian-American favorites including pasta, sausage and peppers, Neapolitan pizza, zeppole, cannoli and gelato. The Galbani Cooking Stage will feature demonstrations throughout the weekend, giving festivalgoers a chance to watch chefs prepare dishes and pick up cooking tips. The published lineup includes Anthony Acampa, Sicilian Oven Chef Andrew, Galbani Chef Marco Sciortino (with special guest Joe Gannascoli from The Sopranos), Cooking with Vinny, Nina's Fresh Bakery and Michelin-starred chef Joe Isidori. Voga wine seminars are also scheduled during the weekend. Can Jupiter make string-cheese history? Saturday brings one of the festival's most unusual attractions. At 4 p.m., organizers are inviting festivalgoers to participate in an event billed as Let's Make Italian Festival History! The goal is to bring people together to simultaneously string string cheese. The public is encouraged to participate, turning a familiar snack into one of the quirkiest moments of the festival's 25th anniversary. entry.summary: A new cheerleading team at Passionate Care Services (PCS) is giving adults with disabilities the opportunity to perform, build friendships and become active participants in community events throughout Palm Beach County. PCS Cheer Beyond Limits was created to provide an inclusive cheerleading experience for adults with special needs. entry.title: Martin County firefighters express concerns over staffing levels at Fire Rescue - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County firefighters express concerns over staffing levels at Fire Rescue    WPBF
entry.article_text: A day after the firefighters' union in Martin County expressed concerns about staffing, the County Administrator is responding by acknowledging the concerns while also saying there's not much that can be done right now. The union raised its concerns in a Thursday social media post, pointing out that the county had canceled an upcoming hiring class of 25 new firefighters even as Fire Rescue is understaffed. "It is about public safety, firefighter working conditions, and ensuring Martin County residents receive the level of emergency services they pay for and deserve," the post said. Don Donaldson, the county administrator for Martin County, acknowledged the union's concerns. "I think the concern of the public is real and legitimate," Donaldson said. Donaldson confirmed that fire rescue is already short-staffed by 17 firefighters and that the hiring class will not proceed as planned. However, he clarified that the class is postponed, not canceled. "I don't want to have to lay somebody off six months right after I hire them," Donaldson said. He explained that the delay is due to uncertainties in the county budget caused by Amendment 3, a measure recently approved by Florida voters that will lower property taxes statewide. Martin County estimates the amendment will result in a $75 million revenue loss over the next two years. Donaldson emphasized the need to assess the budget before committing to new hires. "What I didn't want to have happen is to fully fund all of our firefighters and then find we have to eliminate a position or two with somebody already in the position," Donaldson said. Donaldson said he hopes to have more clarification on the hiring of firefighters within the next few months. entry.title: 911 caller said Palm City man was chasing her with guns, newly released video shows - cw34.com
entry.summary: 911 caller said Palm City man was chasing her with guns, newly released video shows    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A woman who called 911 during a Palm City standoff told dispatchers a man was chasing her with guns and had fired them, according to the call transcript released through a public records request. Please, quickly, the woman said at the start of the call. She told the dispatcher she was running down the street and that the man was so drunk and had tried to get into a car. The call adds detail to the September standoff involving Darrel Abbey, which lasted several hours and brought Martin County Sheriff’s Office deputies, SWAT team members and hostage negotiators to the home. In an earlier report, investigators said Abbey allegedly threatened his ex-girlfriend and pointed a gun at her. The woman told the dispatcher Abbey had put a gun to his head and pulled the trigger about an hour and a half earlier. She said the gun did not fire and that he was not in a good state of mind. As she ran, the caller said Abbey turned around and headed back toward the home. She stopped on the side of the road, where she said another woman had pulled over to help her. The caller also told dispatchers there were multiple guns at the property, though she was unsure whether they were inside the house, in a vehicle or in an RV. Newly released sheriff’s office video shows deputies and a tactical vehicle at the property during the response. The footage is partially obscured, and the provided clip does not clearly show Abbey or the events described in the 911 call. See also: 18-year-old dies after being struck by car in St. Lucie County; family raises concerns According to the arrest report, Abbey’s ex-girlfriend went to his home after their breakup. She told investigators he appeared intoxicated and had a rifle in his Tesla and a 10 mm handgun in his shorts. The report says he brought the guns inside, yelled at her and pointed a gun at her several times. It also says he later tried to get into his vehicle and reached for her phone when he realized she was recording. She ran down the road and called 911. Deputies later tried to contact Abbey at the home, but he refused to open the door or speak with them, according to the arrest report. He was booked into the Martin County Jail without bond on charges including battery and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill. The report also identifies him as a convicted felon with a prior vehicular assault conviction in Washington state.

entry.title: 3,000 walkers fill downtown West Palm Beach for Heart Walk
entry.summary: Thousands of people dressed in red filled downtown West Palm Beach for this years American Heart Association Heart Walk, taking steps to support a cause that touches many families across the community. About 3,000 people took part in the event, which brings together survivors, families and supporters to raise awareness about heart disease and stroke. WATCH: 3,000 walkers fill downtown West Palm Beach for Heart Walk 3,000 walkers fill downtown West Palm Beach for Heart Walk WPTV is a proud sponsor of the Heart Walk, and WPTVs Ashley Glass served as emcee for this years event. For some of the families walking, the mission is deeply personal. WPTVs Christy Waite has been connecting with the family of a young girl named Blake, whose health journey has included heart failure and multiple open-heart surgeries. Before Blake was born, her parents learned she had a heart condition that would lead to multiple heart surgeries. When Blake was just 14 months old, she became very sick. 'She was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, and that put her heart into heart failure, so she had to have open-heart surgery as soon as possible,' her mom, Devin Aubrey, said. Unfortunately, the surgery didn't work, and a few months later Blake had her second open-heart surgery. Doctors put in a mechanical valve to help her heart open and close. As Blake continues to grow, so does her heart, but not the valve. When she is a little older, she will need to have another surgery to fix it. Blake's family formed Team Blake to give back and raise money through the Heart Walk. This year, Team Blake raised $10,000, surpassing the amount the team raised last year. Team Blake wasnt the only one celebrating a fundraising milestone. This years Heart Walk raised more than $1.4 million, setting a new fundraising record. For the walkers who filled downtown West Palm Beach, each step represented a different story, from survivors celebrating how far theyve come to families walking in support of someone they love.

Southbound lanes of Interstate 95 at Mile Marker 128 were closed at 7:45 a.m. near Okeechobee Road, which is State Road 70. entry.title: This not-so-little piggy went rogue! 250-pound boar hog found in Vero Beach - WPEC
entry.summary: This not-so-little piggy went rogue! 250-pound boar hog found in Vero Beach    WPEC
entry.article_text: Somebody's hog has gone rogue, and now Indian River County deputies are trying to bring home the bacon all 250 pounds of it. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office is searching for the owner of a hefty domestic boar hog found in the 5600 block of 69th Street. Weighing an estimated 200 to 250 pounds, the four-legged wanderer is currently being housed safely at the sheriff's office farm while deputies work to track down his owner. See also: Indian River County deputies tussle with alligator displaced by heavy flooding But before anyone can claim the hefty hog, they'll need to prove he's theirs. The sheriff's office is asking anyone who recognizes the animal to contact deputies with a photo or description to verify ownership. For now, the hog is safe and sound at the sheriff's office farm, presumably unaware he's the subject of a countywide search. Anyone who believes the boar belongs to them should contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office.

Lucie County court records. The judge denied the defense’s request for a reduced sentence. O’Hara will receive credit for 3,341 days already served. Fort Pierce police found Bates on a rear patio at an apartment complex at 601 Avenue B on June 12, 2020, with a knife in his neck. He later died during surgery at Lawnwood Hospital. According to the arrest affidavit, a witness told investigators O’Hara accused Bates of being a child rapist before stabbing him. Another witness said she saw O’Hara’s arm move toward Bates’ neck, then saw the knife in Bates’ neck as O’Hara left. Those were witness accounts recorded in the affidavit. See also: 13 state attorneys general ask Supreme Court to uphold Florida's Stop WOKE Act Police said O’Hara fled the scene and was arrested at an Anytime Fitness on Orange Avenue. He denied stabbing Bates during an interview with investigators, the affidavit says.

That there's still kids out there that are still diagnosed." The free screenings are available for children and young adults ages 5 to 20 and include an electrocardiogram (EKG) and a check of vital signs. A cardiologist reviews the results, and an Echocardiogram is available if needed. The Lalloos said close to 650 children have signed up for this year's event. Appointments are booked, but families can call to ask about the waiting list. Organizers said they'll try to fill openings if someone cancels or doesn't show up. Jessica's parents hope their efforts will prevent other families from experiencing a loss like theirs. "The one child could be the next president of our country. It could be the person who invents the cure for cancer. So, every life is important. Children should not die like this," Ray Lalloo said. The event will take place Saturday from 8 a.m. Lucie County Health Department, 5150 NW Milner Drive, Port St. The number to call for scheduling is 772-462-3800. Trump International Airport, but another cancellation awaited them."To have taken the shuttle bus, the train, the shuttle bus ... and then to get here and it's canceled again," Karen Matthews said.She summed up the experience simply: "This is really frustrating."Ron Matthews said the couple had not had a chance to eat during their lengthy trip."It's been kind of rough," he said. entry.title: 911 caller said Palm City man was chasing her with guns, newly released video shows - cw34.com
entry.summary: 911 caller said Palm City man was chasing her with guns, newly released video shows    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A woman who called 911 during a Palm City standoff told dispatchers a man was chasing her with guns and had fired them, according to the call transcript released through a public records request. Please, quickly, the woman said at the start of the call. She told the dispatcher she was running down the street and that the man was so drunk and had tried to get into a car. The call adds detail to the September standoff involving Darrel Abbey, which lasted several hours and brought Martin County Sheriff’s Office deputies, SWAT team members and hostage negotiators to the home. In an earlier report, investigators said Abbey allegedly threatened his ex-girlfriend and pointed a gun at her. The woman told the dispatcher Abbey had put a gun to his head and pulled the trigger about an hour and a half earlier. She said the gun did not fire and that he was not in a good state of mind. As she ran, the caller said Abbey turned around and headed back toward the home. She stopped on the side of the road, where she said another woman had pulled over to help her. The caller also told dispatchers there were multiple guns at the property, though she was unsure whether they were inside the house, in a vehicle or in an RV. Newly released sheriff’s office video shows deputies and a tactical vehicle at the property during the response. The footage is partially obscured, and the provided clip does not clearly show Abbey or the events described in the 911 call. See also: 18-year-old dies after being struck by car in St. Lucie County; family raises concerns According to the arrest report, Abbey’s ex-girlfriend went to his home after their breakup. She told investigators he appeared intoxicated and had a rifle in his Tesla and a 10 mm handgun in his shorts. The report says he brought the guns inside, yelled at her and pointed a gun at her several times. It also says he later tried to get into his vehicle and reached for her phone when he realized she was recording. She ran down the road and called 911. Deputies later tried to contact Abbey at the home, but he refused to open the door or speak with them, according to the arrest report. He was booked into the Martin County Jail without bond on charges including battery and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill. The report also identifies him as a convicted felon with a prior vehicular assault conviction in Washington state.

entry.summary: Playing sports can get expensive, especially when you have to pay for all the gear. But one high school student is finding a creative way to combine her favorite sport and giving back. Ella Axtell is a senior at The Benjamin School and founded 'Gear for Goals.' WATCH: High school senior scores big by giving soccer gear to kids in need High school senior scores big by giving soccer gear to kids in need 'Gear for Goals is an organization that I go and take used and new soccer gear and equipment, and I take it to kids who are less fortunate,' Axtell said. Axtell donates the soccer gear to centers like Place of Hope, Family First and Quantum House. 'They come in there using their wheelchairs. We play soccer with them in any way that they are. We equip them and it's crazy, they love it so much. They always say how it's able to give them a place to play and give them an advantage to play,' Axtell said. She also hosts clinics to teach kids how to play. 'I love it. I honestly love it because I really do think every kid should have the chance to play and I don't want one kid not to be able to if they don't have the gear,' Axtell said. Gear for Goals is not only helping young athletes in Palm Beach County, but across the world. 'We've gone all over. I went to Costa Rica internationally with St. Mark's and I held four days in that week. I held soccer clinics and each kid got a full entire kit from shirts to cleats,' Axtell said. Axtell said when she came up with the idea for Gear for Goals, she started posting online. We have an Instagram called @ Gear_for_goals , and I send out flyers and post all the time about it. And then I started reaching out to other places that I could have boxes at. So I had one at Palm Beach Gardens Rec Center, Axtell said. I actually was able to host a soccer drive for dressing for charity at St. Mark's, and we raised money, and got a bunch of money for that. And I just spread the word, have an Amazon wish list. I'm just emailing, emailing, emailing. Donations have flooded in, with people giving new and slightly used soccer gear or buying from her online equipment wishlist. 'I just want to continue it. I want to continue it through college. I want to keep going, see how big we can grow and hopefully one day we'll be so big that we'll have clinics all over the world,' Axtell said. While helping kids score goals, Axtell says her goal is to grow the organization. She says they're always looking for donations and volunteers. To donate or learn

entry.title: Port St. Lucie family offers free heart screenings to honor late daughter - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie family offers free heart screenings to honor late daughter    WPBF
entry.article_text: The parents of Jessica Clinton, a Port St. Lucie teen who died of cardiac arrest in 2003, are hosting a free heart screening event this Saturday at the St. Lucie County Health Department to raise awareness about children's heart health. Jessica Clinton's parents Ray and Cheryl Lalloo are preparing for the event, which is expected to draw about 600 children. He stressed the importance of identifying heart problems early. "You hear it all the time. Kids go to sleep, parents come in the morning, they're not awake, and it's now just infants, or SIDS, it's kids that are 10, 12, 13 years old," Ray Lalloo said. Jessica was 17 years old and at cheerleading practice at St. Lucie West Centennial High School when she went into cardiac arrest. At the time, there were no automated external defibrillators (AEDs) on campus, and Jessica died that day. Her parents said she had undergone two sports physicals in the months before her death, but no heart problem was detected. In response to their loss, Jessica's parents founded the Jessica Clinton MVP Foundation and began offering heart screenings 17 years ago. They said the screenings have helped identify previously undiagnosed heart conditions. Last year, they said about 19 children learned they had a condition that had not been detected before. "We've had a couple of kids with pretty significant diagnoses. You know, things like syndrome, the really bad ones, you know," Ray Lalloo said. Cheryl Lalloo is grateful they were able to offer free screenings. "Blessed is the word, Cheryl Lalloo said. "It makes us feel like we also have a lot more work to do. That there's still kids out there that are still diagnosed." The free screenings are available for children and young adults ages 5 to 20 and include an electrocardiogram (EKG) and a check of vital signs. A cardiologist reviews the results, and an Echocardiogram is available if needed. The Lalloos said close to 650 children have signed up for this year's event. Appointments are booked, but families can call to ask about the waiting list. Organizers said they'll try to fill openings if someone cancels or doesn't show up. Jessica's parents hope their efforts will prevent other families from experiencing a loss like theirs. "The one child could be the next president of our country. It could be the person who invents the cure for cancer. So, every life is important. Children should not die like this," Ray Lalloo said. The event will take place Saturday from 8 a.m. Lucie County Health Department, 5150 NW Milner Drive, Port St. The number to call for scheduling is 772-462-3800. For now, the hog is safe and sound at the sheriff's office farm, presumably unaware he's the subject of a countywide search. Anyone who believes the boar belongs to them should contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office.

entry.title: Man dies after going 101 mph, crashing into palm trees in Fort Pierce in I-95 police chase - WPBF
entry.summary: Man dies after going 101 mph, crashing into palm trees in Fort Pierce in I-95 police chase    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 59-year-old DeLand man died when he crashed into palm trees off Interstate 95 after being pursued by Florida Highway Patrol troopers at a high rate of speed on Saturday morning in Fort Pierce. Southbound lanes of Interstate 95 at Mile Marker 128 were closed at 7:45 a.m. near Okeechobee Road, which is State Road 70. A 2020 Volvo S60 was traveling southbound three miles away at Mile Marker 141 at a high rate of speed, according to FHP. A trooper was stationary on the southbound side and clocked the vehicle at 101 miles per hour, FHP said. Troopers attempted to intercept the driver for the traffic violation, but he failed to stop and continued to travel southbound at a high rate of speed, maneuvering in and out of traffic and utilizing the paved shoulders. A trooper attempted a PIT maneuver (Precision Immobilization Technique), which was unsuccessful, north of State Road 70. The driver continued traveling south at a high rate of speed and entered the inside paved shoulder and continued into the grass median, FHP said. The vehicle struck several large palm trees with the left front/driver’s side compartment. He was ejected and was pronounced deceased at the scene, FHP said. entry.summary: Florida’s Turnpike closed in both directions in Martin County; truck jackknifed    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A crash involving a tractor-trailer and a pickup truck closed all northbound lanes of Florida’s Turnpike near Mile Marker 137 in Palm City on Friday, according to Martin County Fire Rescue. Both drivers were safe, and no injuries were reported. Fire rescue, the Martin County Sheriff’s Office and Florida Highway Patrol were working to clear debris from the roadway. The crash happened just before 11 a.m. Northbound traffic was closed from before Exit 133 for Stuart and Martin Downs Boulevard (State Road 714) to before Mile Marker 137. A separate police activity closure extended from before Mile Marker 130 to Exit 133, and the northbound on-ramp was also closed. Southbound, a jackknifed truck was causing congestion from before Mile Marker 139 to before Mile Marker 137, according to Florida 511. Drivers were advised to take alternate routes and expect delays. entry.title: Stuart Air Show celebrates 37th year at Witham Field in Martin County - WFLX
entry.summary: Stuart Air Show celebrates 37th year at Witham Field in Martin County    WFLX
entry.article_text: The Stuart Air Show is preparing to take flight at Witham Field, bringing aircraft, crowds and heavier traffic to the Stuart area. The air show is celebrating its 37th year at Witham Field on Friday and this year’s event will feature the F-16 demo team along with a variety of other aircraft. The show runs through Sunday, Nov. Among those participating is Maj. Taylor Hiester, the United States Air Force F-16 Viper Demonstration Team Commander and Pilot stationed at Shaw Air Force Base in Sumter, South Carolina. “I’ve been in the Air Force for 11 years now, and it’s been a dream come true for the last three years to serve, not just as a military officer first, but fighter pilot second,” Hiester told WFLX Anchor Mike Trim. “To be the American fighter pilot that gets to connect the American people with the people that do their business around the world on their behalf, is very special.” The 37th annual air show features F-16s, large military planes, ghost riders, aerobatic planes and skydivers, along with games and food for families. “It’s for me, my last performance and for a lot of performers, it’s that it’s the close out of the year,” Hiester told WFLX. “So, it is a wonderful cocktail of emotions that come together that make a fantastic show for the people of Florida, and I think that the people are going to notice that there’s something special.” Beyond the flight demonstrations, the event also focused on education and STEM classes WFLX First Alert Weather Meteorologist Kate Wentzel spoke with students from the aerospace club from Jupiter Christian, along with students from the Parker area, the Virginia Beach area, Fort Pierce and around the Treasure Coast. “In the air show, they want to partner with all of these school groups and organizations, because really it empowers them and inspires them to go into aviation-related careers,” Wentzel said. Weather plays a critical role in aviation, and the students learned how it affects pilots. “We talked about winds, how that impacts pilots. Pilots want to take off into the wind, because the wind blowing over the wings, gives them better lift and a faster lift speed,” Wentzel said. “They also want to land into the wind, because if they have a tailwind pushing them too strong, it can make it difficult for the pilot to have a controlled landing.” Students also learned how icing can impact aircraft at high altitudes and near thunderstorms. Aircraft are supposed to stay 20 miles away from severe thunderstorms at all times, because that is where big updrafts and gusty winds develop, Wentzel said. Conditions are expected to be clear and breezy this evening, making for good viewing of the Stuart Air Show.

entry.title: Jensen Beach neighbors help families rebuild weeks after historic flooding
entry.summary: Weeks after historic flooding devastated homes in Jensen Beach, Martin County families are still cleaning up and rebuilding, with volunteers, churches, firefighters, contractors and local leaders joining the recovery effort. Water marks remain visible on some homes, showing how high floodwaters rose. Residents are now removing damaged drywall, clearing debris and collecting donated supplies while seeking financial assistance and answers about the area's drainage systems. Jensen Beach families rebuild as neighbors rally after historic flooding Neighbors step in to help Jensen Beach families Before-and-after video from the Jensen Beach neighborhood shows the extent of the flooding, which left several homes under feet of water. Weeks later, homeowner Lisa Marie French said cleaning up has been a major undertaking. We first told you about French's circumstances last week. 'Its a lot of work. You first have to empty the houses,' French said. 'We have to clean the houses; they're filled with mold, we have to take the drywall out.' French, whose home was impacted by the flooding, has also helped coordinate community cleanup efforts alongside Christ of Church, Family Church and other organizations. She said neighbors and other volunteers have repeatedly shown up asking what families need and then immediately gotten to work. 'People have been just coming and just hands-on,' French said. 'People are like, 'Hey, are you taking donations? What do you need?' And they get out of their cars, and they start working, and that's our neighbors. Its pretty amazing.' Residents seek answers about flooding and drainage As cleanup continues, residents say they also want answers about what contributed to the severe flooding. entry.title: Missed kicks doom Miami Dolphins in 24-22 loss to Indianapolis Colts
entry.summary: The Indianapolis Colts got the respite they needed. After losing five straight and enduring three weeks of tumult, they finally celebrated a victory. Daniel Jones threw for one score, Seth McGowan ran for another and Adetomiwa Adebawore recovered a fumble for a touchdown on Sunday as the Colts held on for a 24-22 victory over the Miami Dolphins to end their skid. 'It definitely feels good to win,' Jones said. 'It's hard to win in the NFL, so you have to enjoy them.' Colts fans didn't seem to enjoy this one much. Some showed up wearing bags over their heads after Indy shipped away two Pro Bowl captains and their top two receivers before the trade deadline. The Colts held onto Jones and star running back Jonathan Taylor, who said goodbye to Indy fans last week only to suit up again and finish with 103 total yards. While he helped the Colts (3-7) rush for 172 yards, Jones was booed loudly during the second half, when he had just one completion beyond the line of scrimmage. Jones was 11 of 22 for 108 yards with two interceptions. Indy was also flagged 13 times, several of which prevented the Colts from sealing the victory sooner. They wound up needing a fourth-down stop with 1:36 left and McGowan's run for a first down on the ensuing possession to close it out. The offense's struggles led to questions about a possible quarterback switch, which coach Shane Steichen quickly shut down because Indy plays Thursday night. 'Yeah, he'll be the starting quarterback this week,' Steichen said of Jones. 'I think we need to continue to get better. There are a lot of things that happen out there every day, self-inflicted wounds for sure, but we've all got to be better.' Kyle McCord had a solid starting debut for Miami (1-8), which lost its third straight. He was 17 of 32 for 209 yards, ran for a score and lost one fumble in place of Malik Willis , who went on injured reserve earlier this week with a groin injury. Ollie Gordon II had 20 carries for 76 yards. Miami missed three kicks, including a 51-yard field goal attempt in the fourth quarter that would have given the Dolphins the lead. 'We've got to make the extra point, and we've got to make the field goal,' coach Jeff Hafley said. 'It's 24-22, we miss an extra point, which forces us to go for 2, and we miss two field goals, that's seven points. We have to make those.' Indy broke a 7-7 tie when Jones found Laquon Treadwell for a 7-yard TD with 39 seconds left in the first half. It was Treadwell's first TD catch since 2021

Haulcy to keep the Colts ahead by two.Dolphins: Miami played without C Aaron Brewer (concussion protocol) and lost DT Zeek Biggers (knee) in the first half. But he finished with 16 carries for 83 yards and two catches for 20 yards, leaving him with 9,999.Dolphins: At Buffalo next Sunday.Colts: Go for a season sweep when they visit Houston on Thursday.

entry.title: High school senior helps young athletes score big by giving soccer gear to kids in need
entry.summary: Playing sports can get expensive, especially when you have to pay for all the gear. But one high school student is finding a creative way to combine her favorite sport and giving back. Ella Axtell is a senior at The Benjamin School and founded 'Gear for Goals.' WATCH: High school senior scores big by giving soccer gear to kids in need High school senior scores big by giving soccer gear to kids in need 'Gear for Goals is an organization that I go and take used and new soccer gear and equipment, and I take it to kids who are less fortunate,' Axtell said. Axtell donates the soccer gear to centers like Place of Hope, Family First and Quantum House. 'They come in there using their wheelchairs. We play soccer with them in any way that they are. We equip them, and it's crazy, they love it so much. They always say how it's able to give them a place to play and give them an advantage to play,' Axtell said. She also hosts clinics to teach kids how to play. 'I love it. I honestly love it because I really do think every kid should have the chance to play, and I don't want one kid not to be able to if they don't have the gear,' Axtell said. Gear for Goals is not only helping young athletes in Palm Beach County, but across the world. 'We've gone all over. I went to Costa Rica internationally with St. Mark's and I held four days in that week. I held soccer clinics and each kid got a full entire kit from shirts to cleats,' Axtell said. Axtell said when she came up with the idea for Gear for Goals, she started posting online. We have an Instagram called @ Gear_for_goals , and I send out flyers and post all the time about it. And then I started reaching out to other places that I could have boxes at. So I had one at Palm Beach Gardens Rec Center, Axtell said. I actually was able to host a soccer drive for dressing for charity at St. Mark's, and we raised money, and got a bunch of money for that. And I just spread the word, have an Amazon wish list. I'm just emailing, emailing, emailing. Donations have flooded in, with people giving new and slightly used soccer gear or buying from her online equipment wishlist. 'I just want to continue it. entry.title: 2 planes collide on the ground at Miami International Airport, minor injuries reported
entry.summary: Federal aviation safety officials on Sunday were investigating a minor collision between two planes at a taxiway intersection at Miami International Airport, where one aircraft's wingtip struck the nose of another, authorities said. Two people reported minor injuries. The accident happened at about 9 p.m. Saturday and involved a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 aircraft with 172 people aboard and a UPS Boeing 767 cargo plane, according to the National Transportation Safety Board and Copa Airlines. The wing of the Copa flight and the nose of the UPS plane collided, the NTSB said. Photos taken at the scene show the UPS plane nose with a horizontal gash on one side and a larger hole in the middle. On audio recorded by ATC.com, a pilot on the UPS plane told air traffic control that he went too far at the intersection and his plane was clipped by the Copa flight. Air traffic control told the UPS pilot that he was supposed to yield to the Copa aircraft. The NTSB said Sunday that preliminary information showed the UPS plane was instructed to give way to the Copa Airlines flight but did not stop. The UPS aircraft had substantial damage, while an assessment of the Copa plane had not been completed, it said. The NTSB said it opened an investigation and expected a preliminary report to be released within 30 days. The Copa plane had just arrived from Panama City and the UPS plane was headed to Bogota, Colombia, officials said. In a statement on social media, Copa called the collision minor and said two of its passengers were treated at the scene for minor injuries. UPS said it was working with authorities to determine what happened. 'We cannot speculate on the details of the incident,' UPS said in a statement. The National Transportation Safety Board is responsible for investigating incidents like this and will control the flow of information.' The mishap came two months after an Amazon cargo plane careened off a runway at Miami International and smashed into a van carrying workers for a company that cleans airplanes, killing five people.

entry.title: Stuart Air Show celebrates 37th year at Witham Field in Martin County - WFLX
entry.summary: Stuart Air Show celebrates 37th year at Witham Field in Martin County    WFLX
entry.article_text: The Stuart Air Show is preparing to take flight at Witham Field, bringing aircraft, crowds and heavier traffic to the Stuart area. The air show is celebrating its 37th year at Witham Field on Friday and this year’s event will feature the F-16 demo team along with a variety of other aircraft. The show runs through Sunday, Nov. Among those participating is Maj. Taylor Hiester, the United States Air Force F-16 Viper Demonstration Team Commander and Pilot stationed at Shaw Air Force Base in Sumter, South Carolina. “I’ve been in the Air Force for 11 years now, and it’s been a dream come true for the last three years to serve, not just as a military officer first, but fighter pilot second,” Hiester told WFLX Anchor Mike Trim. “To be the American fighter pilot that gets to connect the American people with the people that do their business around the world on their behalf, is very special.” The 37th annual air show features F-16s, large military planes, ghost riders, aerobatic planes and skydivers, along with games and food for families. “It’s for me, my last performance and for a lot of performers, it’s that it’s the close out of the year,” Hiester told WFLX. “So, it is a wonderful cocktail of emotions that come together that make a fantastic show for the people of Florida, and I think that the people are going to notice that there’s something special.” Beyond the flight demonstrations, the event also focused on education and STEM classes WFLX First Alert Weather Meteorologist Kate Wentzel spoke with students from the aerospace club from Jupiter Christian, along with students from the Parker area, the Virginia Beach area, Fort Pierce and around the Treasure Coast. “In the air show, they want to partner with all of these school groups and organizations, because really it empowers them and inspires them to go into aviation-related careers,” Wentzel said. Weather plays a critical role in aviation, and the students learned how it affects pilots. “We talked about winds, how that impacts pilots. Pilots want to take off into the wind, because the wind blowing over the wings, gives them better lift and a faster lift speed,” Wentzel said. “They also want to land into the wind, because if they have a tailwind pushing them too strong, it can make it difficult for the pilot to have a controlled landing.” Students also learned how icing can impact aircraft at high altitudes and near thunderstorms. Aircraft are supposed to stay 20 miles away from severe thunderstorms at all times, because that is where big updrafts and gusty winds develop, Wentzel said. Conditions are expected to be clear and breezy this evening, making for good viewing of the Stuart Air Show.

entry.title: 37th Stuart Air Show draws big crowds for picture-perfect weekend
entry.summary: The 37th Stuart Air Show brought aviation fans young and old together for a picture-perfect weekend filled with aircraft, family traditions, and appreciation for veterans. Organizers said the weekend got off to a strong start Friday night with a drone and fireworks show and continued with large crowds throughout the weekend. Stuart Air Show has had an amazing weekend Friday night with our drone and fireworks show. We had a great turnout, Chrissy Valvano said. Sunday, were looking at a record turnout for Veterans Appreciation Day, and this weather could not be better. For some families, attending the Stuart Air Show has become a tradition passed down through the years. The Stuart Air Show has been a part of our community for many years, Sarah Naylor said. We have many memories of coming in the past, as long as I can remember. For younger aviation fans Wyatt and Ivy Rotan, some of the biggest attractions were the military aircraft. I like coming to the Stuart Air Show because I like to see the C-17 and the F-16 fly, Wyatt said. I like seeing the C-17, Ivy added. The event also gave young people a chance to learn more about aviation while honoring those who served. You get to have a lot of fun around here, just going around and seeing a bunch of planes, John Gefell said. Also because Im working on my aviation merit badge as a Boy Scout and my grandpa was a veteran, so its just real fun to come out here and just have a lot of fun. With beautiful weather and a strong turnout, the 37th Stuart Air Show once again brought the community together, giving longtime fans and a new generation of aviation enthusiasts a weekend to remember.

entry.article_text: Home Schools InnovatED Phase 2 town hall set for Monday at Sebastian River Middle by Tina Hodges Nov 15, 2026 / 12:23 PM A A A A Reset InnovatED (School District of IRC) Share on Twitter Share via Email SEBASTIAN — The School District of Indian River County will hold an InnovatED Phase 2 town hall Monday, November 16, from 5:30 to 6:30 p.m. at Sebastian River Middle School to gather public feedback on two facility proposals still under consideration. District officials have invited families, staff, and community members to hear details, ask questions, and share thoughts on the plans. The two proposals focus on a future home for Wabasso School that would add capacity and specialized learning spaces, and on creating a connected arts pathway in Sebastian. Both remain under review, with School Board consideration expected in December. Wabasso School currently serves students with specialized needs on U.S. District leaders have previously described the campus as at capacity and have discussed relocating the program to the former Glendale Elementary site in Vero Beach to allow room for growth and more tailored spaces for life skills and independent learning. The arts pathway proposal involves Sebastian Elementary School of the Arts, which officials have said could share the Sebastian River Middle School campus as a separate school while maintaining its own identity. This is the latest in a series of InnovatED community sessions. Phase 1 of the initiative, which included several school relocations, shared campuses, and boundary adjustments, took effect for the 2026-27 school year after School Board approval in December 2025. The original Sebastian River Middle School town hall for Phase 2 was postponed from Nov. Residents who cannot attend can still submit questions or comments. Share input with the planning team. entry.title: The secret to a perfect Thanksgiving turkey? Okeechobee Steakhouse says it's butter
entry.summary: If you've ever admired a perfectly golden Thanksgiving turkey and wondered how professional chefs make it look so good, Okeechobee Steakhouse co-owner Ralph Lewis has a surprisingly simple answer. 'It's butter.' And not just a little butter. During a recent Thanksgiving cooking demonstration at Okeechobee Prime Meat Market, Lewis stood beside a giant inflatable stick of butter, worked from a table piled high with butter and seasonings, and even pulled a backup rubber stick of butter from his pocket. For Lewis, butter isn't simply an ingredient. It's the foundation of a great Thanksgiving turkey. 'Are you really supposed to have a budget with butter?' Lewis joked. 'Those two words do not go together.' The Butter Trick That Makes The Difference According to Lewis, the biggest mistake many home cooks make is putting all of their butter on the outside of the bird. Instead, he recommends carefully separating the skin from the breast meat and creating pockets beneath the skin. Once those pockets are created, it's time to start adding butter. Lots of butter. 'You just want to keep working it in there,' Lewis said. 'You can't put enough. You can't put too much. That's impossible, literally impossible, and that's a chef's code.' As the turkey cooks, the butter melts beneath the skin, helping keep the meat moist while contributing to the rich color and flavor many Thanksgiving hosts are trying to achieve. After working butter beneath the skin, Lewis also coats the outside of the turkey before adding seasoning. Pro Tip: Season The Butter First One of the most useful tips Lewis shared involves seasoning the butter before it ever touches the bird. Start by taking butter out of the refrigerator and allowing it to soften to room temperature. Then combine the softened butter with herbs and seasonings such as: Kosher salt Freshly ground black pepper Thyme Rosemary Sage Mix everything together until it forms a seasoned compound butter. Then spread that butter beneath the skin and across the exterior of the turkey. By combining the herbs and seasoning directly into the butter, the flavors are distributed more evenly throughout the turkey as it cooks. entry.title: Port St. Lucie family offers free heart screenings to honor late daughter - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie family offers free heart screenings to honor late daughter    WPBF
entry.article_text: The parents of Jessica Clinton, a Port St. Lucie teen who died of cardiac arrest in 2003, are hosting a free heart screening event this Saturday at the St. Lucie County Health Department to raise awareness about children's heart health. Jessica Clinton's parents Ray and Cheryl Lalloo are preparing for the event, which is expected to draw about 600 children. He stressed the importance of identifying heart problems early. "You hear it all the time. Kids go to sleep, parents come in the morning, they're not awake, and it's now just infants, or SIDS, it's kids that are 10, 12, 13 years old," Ray Lalloo said. Jessica was 17 years old and at cheerleading practice at St. Lucie West Centennial High School when she went into cardiac arrest. At the time, there were no automated external defibrillators (AEDs) on campus, and Jessica died that day. Her parents said she had undergone two sports physicals in the months before her death, but no heart problem was detected. In response to their loss, Jessica's parents founded the Jessica Clinton MVP Foundation and began offering heart screenings 17 years ago. They said the screenings have helped identify previously undiagnosed heart conditions. Last year, they said about 19 children learned they had a condition that had not been detected before. "We've had a couple of kids with pretty significant diagnoses. You know, things like syndrome, the really bad ones, you know," Ray Lalloo said. Cheryl Lalloo is grateful they were able to offer free screenings. "Blessed is the word, Cheryl Lalloo said. "It makes us feel like we also have a lot more work to do. That there's still kids out there that are still diagnosed." The free screenings are available for children and young adults ages 5 to 20 and include an electrocardiogram (EKG) and a check of vital signs. A cardiologist reviews the results, and an Echocardiogram is available if needed. The Lalloos said close to 650 children have signed up for this year's event. Appointments are booked, but families can call to ask about the waiting list. Organizers said they'll try to fill openings if someone cancels or doesn't show up. Jessica's parents hope their efforts will prevent other families from experiencing a loss like theirs. "The one child could be the next president of our country. It could be the person who invents the cure for cancer. So, every life is important. Children should not die like this," Ray Lalloo said. entry.title: 37th Stuart Air Show draws big crowds for picture-perfect weekend
entry.summary: The 37th Stuart Air Show brought aviation fans young and old together for a picture-perfect weekend filled with aircraft, family traditions, and appreciation for veterans. Organizers said the weekend got off to a strong start Friday night with a drone and fireworks show and continued with large crowds throughout the weekend. 'Stuart Air Show has had an amazing weekend Friday night with our drone and fireworks show. We had a great turnout,' Chrissy Valvano said. 'Sunday, we're looking at a record turnout for Veterans Appreciation Day, and this weather could not be better.' For some families, attending the Stuart Air Show has become a tradition passed down through the years. 'The Stuart Air Show has been a part of our community for many years,' Sarah Naylor said. 'We have many memories of coming in the past, as long as I can remember.' For younger aviation fans Wyatt and Ivy Rotan, some of the biggest attractions were the military aircraft. 'I like coming to the Stuart Air Show because I like to see the C-17 and the F-16 fly,' Wyatt said. 'I like seeing the C-17,' Ivy added. The event also gave young people a chance to learn more about aviation while honoring those who served. 'You get to have a lot of fun around here, just going around and seeing a bunch of planes,' John Gefell said. 'Also, because I'm working on my aviation merit badge as a Boy Scout and my grandpa was a veteran, so its just real fun to come out here and just have a lot of fun.' With beautiful weather and a strong turnout, the 37th Stuart Air Show once again brought the community together, giving longtime fans and a new generation of aviation enthusiasts a weekend to remember.

entry.title: The secret to a perfect Thanksgiving turkey? Okeechobee Steakhouse says it's butter
entry.summary: If you've ever admired a perfectly golden Thanksgiving turkey and wondered how professional chefs make it look so good, Okeechobee Steakhouse co-owner Ralph Lewis has a surprisingly simple answer. 'It's butter.' And not just a little butter. Secret to a golden Thanksgiving turkey? Butter, butter and more butter During a recent Thanksgiving cooking demonstration at Okeechobee Prime Meat Market, Lewis stood beside a giant inflatable stick of butter, worked from a table piled high with butter and seasonings, and even pulled a backup rubber stick of butter from his pocket. For Lewis, butter isn't simply an ingredient. It's the foundation of a great Thanksgiving turkey. 'Are you really supposed to have a budget with butter?' Lewis joked. 'Those two words do not go together.' The Butter Trick That Makes The Difference According to Lewis, the biggest mistake many home cooks make is putting all of their butter on the outside of the bird. Instead, he recommends carefully separating the skin from the breast meat and creating pockets beneath the skin. Once those pockets are created, it's time to start adding butter. Lots of butter. 'You just want to keep working it in there,' Lewis said. 'You can't put enough. You can't put too much. That's impossible, literally impossible, and that's a chef's code.' As the turkey cooks, the butter melts beneath the skin, helping keep the meat moist while contributing to the rich color and flavor many Thanksgiving hosts are trying to achieve. After working butter beneath the skin, Lewis also coats the outside of the turkey before adding seasoning. Pro Tip: Season The Butter First One of the most useful tips Lewis shared involves seasoning the butter before it ever touches the bird. Start by taking butter out of the refrigerator and allowing it to soften to room temperature. Then combine the softened butter with herbs and seasonings such as: Kosher salt Freshly ground black pepper Thyme Rosemary Sage Mix everything together until it forms a seasoned compound butter. Then spread that butter beneath the skin and across the exterior of the turkey. By combining the herbs and seasoning directly into the butter, the flavors are distributed more evenly throughout the turkey as it cooks. entry.article_text: Everyone knows Las Vegas as Sin City, but Florida has its own share of cities on WalletHub’s list of America’s most sinful places. 6 in WalletHub’s 2026 sinful cities study, while Port St. Lucie landed near the bottom. The ranking comes as Grand Theft Auto VI brings players back to a Florida-inspired Vice City. Florida’s connection to fictional Vice City is also in the spotlight ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI, scheduled for release Nov. The game returns to a Miami-inspired setting within the fictional state of Leonida. Miami recently added a giant pink Welcome to Vice City sign atop the Kaseya Center as part of a deal with game developer Rockstar Games. County officials said the agreement is expected to bring in nearly $1 million in revenue and create marketing opportunities. WalletHub compared 182 U.S. cities using measures grouped into seven categories, including crime, gambling, drinking, charitable giving and adult entertainment. The ranking is based on selected city-level indicators, not a judgment about individual residents. RELATED: Playboy plans $12.5M takeover of Miami Beach hotel for exclusive members-only club Among Florida cities, Miami ranked highest, with a WalletHub Vice Index score of 52.07. Tampa ranked 29th, Fort Lauderdale 32nd and Jacksonville 35th. Here’s how the Florida cities included in the report ranked: Miami: No. 177 WalletHub’s category rankings show how a city’s overall position can combine very different measures. Miami ranked sixth for jealousy and eighth for lust, but 106th for anger and hatred. Orlando ranked first for jealousy, while Tampa tied for the most adult entertainment establishments per capita. WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo said the ranking combines behaviors that can have very different effects. Some, such as violent crime and identity theft, are harmful in themselves, while others, including alcohol use and gambling, can become damaging when they are not kept under control, he said. The report also lists a panel of academics, including a Lynn University associate professor. How WalletHub ranked the cities WalletHub compared the 150 most populated U.S. cities and at least two of the most populated cities in each state. Its 37 measures were grouped into seven categories: anger and hatred, jealousy, excesses and vices, greed, lust, vanity and laziness. The measures included violent crime, excessive drinking, gambling problems, charitable donations, adult entertainment establishments, tanning salons and the share of adults who do not exercise. See also: Armed woman shot, killed by deputy outside popular Florida bar after confrontation Each measure received a score on a 100-point scale, with higher scores indicating more of the behavior WalletHub was measuring. The company calculated weighted averages to create each city’s overall Vice Index and ranking. Data were collected through Oct. 19, 2026, from sources including federal agencies, public health organizations, Google and Yelp. The 10 highest-ranked cities Las Vegas, Nevada Houston, Texas Los Angeles, California Philadelphia, Pennsylvania Atlanta, Georgia Miami, Florida Dallas, Texas Denver, Colorado Phoenix, Arizona St. Louis, Missouri The 10 lowest-ranked cities WalletHub ranked these cities lowest on its index, with No. Bridgeport, Connecticut 176. entry.summary: Federal dollars are coming to help local parents continue their college education while dealing with the high cost of childcare. U.S. Rep. Lois Frankel, D-Fla., announced Monday a $500,000 annual grant, funded for the next four years, designed to help student parents at Palm Beach State College. WATCH REPORT BELOW: $2M grant targets student childcare costs for Palm Beach State College parents Those accepted into the program based on income guidelines will pay on a sliding scale, anywhere from nothing to $160 a month. 'Students shouldnt have to choose between an uplifting career and taking care of their children, and this type of grant gives them the opportunity to do both,' Frankel said. Frankel says the average cost of child care in Palm Beach County is around $13,000 annually. The plan is to get 75 parents initially enrolled. Palm Beach State College President Ava Parker says 75% of the students on campus attend college part-time and need to work, so this assistance will allow the parents to find a childcare center close to their home.

entry.title: PBSO detectives seek to identify woman who took envelope with cash from Dollar Tree in Wellington
entry.summary: Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office detectives are asking for the public's assistance in identifying a woman who was seen on video taking a bank envelope containing cash that was left on the counter at a Dollar Tree in Wellington. The incident occurred on Sept. 4 at around 12:15 p.m. at the Dollar Tree located at 10510 Forest Hill Blvd. According to PBSO, the victim made a purchase at the Dollar Tree and left a blue bank envelope containing $500 on the counter. The woman was captured on video picking up the envelope and walking out of the store with it, making no attempt to return the envelope to store employees, deputies said. The woman was wearing gray leggings and a gray T-shirt and carrying a denim handbag. entry.title: Heavy rain, flooding possible in West Palm Beach this week as city extends state of emergency
entry.summary: West Palm Beach residents are being urged to prepare for another round of heavy rain and possible flooding this week while parts of the city are still recovering from historic rainfall earlier this month. The city said Monday that heavy rainfall and isolated flash flooding are possible from Tuesday through Thursday. According to information provided by the city from the National Weather Service, there is a 40% to 60% chance that 2 to 4 inches of rain could fall across much of South Florida's east coast, with significantly higher amounts possible in isolated locations. Additional rain could worsen flooding in areas where the ground remains saturated from the Nov. 1-2 flooding, particularly in low-lying neighborhoods. Mayor Keith James has extended West Palm Beach's local state of emergency through Sunday, Nov. 22. City officials said the extension allows West Palm Beach to continue emergency measures, coordinate resources and assist residents affected by the flooding. West Palm Beach prepares for additional flooding City crews and emergency personnel are continuing recovery work while preparing for the possibility of more flooding. According to the city, crews are monitoring affected neighborhoods and inspecting and clearing city-maintained storm drain grates. Officials are also evaluating whether garbage, recycling and yard waste collection can be accelerated in western communities hit hardest by the recent flooding to reduce the risk of additional service disruptions. The city is continuing to operate an auxiliary pumping station to lower water levels in the Apoxee Reserve. Water-control structures at Grassy Waters are also being managed to increase available storage capacity ahead of additional rainfall. City staff are meeting daily with regional partners to monitor water levels, review pumping operations and assess the capacity of the drainage system. How residents should prepare for heavy rain West Palm Beach officials are asking residents to prepare now in case flooding makes travel difficult. Residents should: Monitor weather forecasts and official city updates. Avoid driving or walking through flooded areas. Use caution around standing water and storm drains. Stock up on drinking water, nonperishable food and necessary medications. Make sure they have baby supplies, pet food and other household essentials they may need if travel becomes difficult.
