The agreement allows state and local law enforcement officers to conduct immigration enforcement activities on ICE's behalf. The 287(g) program has been around for 30 years.WATCH REPORT BELOW: "(It's) basically a program that if someone came into the jail, then the jail could run their information through an immigration database and alert ICE if they had an immigration detainer or some civil immigration issue, and then ICE could come and pick them up," said Felicity Rose, vice president of research and policy at fwd.us, a bipartisan advocacy organization that focuses on immigration and criminal justice. Rose and her team have been tracking the Trump administration's use of 287(g) agreements. They recently published a report using public and leaked records to estimate how much money local law enforcement agencies are getting from ICE in exchange for participating in 287(g)."Those partnerships are both sending billions of dollars to state and local law enforcement with very little oversight," Rose said.I asked Rose for her data on each sheriff's office in our five-county viewing area. In Palm Beach County, the report estimates more than $16 million in available funding for fiscal year 2026. In Martin County, the estimate is nearly $1.8 million, along with $5.3 million in St. Lucie County, $1.7 million in Okeechobee County and $880,000 in Indian River County.PREVIOUS COVERAGE: Several local police departments are enrolled in 287(g) program"After the so-called One Big Beautiful Bill Act in the summer of 2025 passed, they gave $191 billion to (the U.S. Department of Homeland Security). One thing they decided to do with that was start paying people who signed up for the task force model," Rose explained.ICE breaks down its 287(g) task force payment structure on its website: initial stipends of $100,000, plus $7,500 per credentialed officer. Then, quarterly stipends of $15,000 per officer per quarter. That's on top of salary reimbursement for officers' time working immigration enforcement, plus "quarterly monetary performance awards based on the successful location of illegal aliens.""That money led to a major change in the number of agencies signing up and, very importantly, the number of arrests that they were making," Rose said.The Florida Department of Law Enforcement tracks 287(g) arrests throughout the state. Their data states that since August 2025, the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office had 361, the Okeechobee County Sheriff's Office carried out 37, Indian River County had 38 and St. Lucie County had 15. The Martin County Sheriff's Office had 1,095 287(g) arrests.The Martin County Sheriff's Office declined an interview for this story, but Sheriff John Budensiek spoke to us in December 2025 about accepting funding to help with immigration detention."I don't think our taxpayers should be taxed again. I think the federal government, if they're going to use us as a tool, should pay for their portion of that," Budensiek said.A spokeswoman for MCSO told me in a statement that "The Martin County Sheriff's Office has not conducted any recent immigration enforcement operations under the 287(g) program. Individuals without lawful immigration status who are arrested on local criminal charges in Martin County are booked into the Martin County Jail. The number of those bookings is substantially lower than the figure you cited."Mariana Blanco and her team at the Guatemalan Maya Center in Lake Worth Beach have also been tracking immigration arrests and working with the families impacted by them."When you begin monetizing these arrests, now you lose sight of the protection of the people, and that's exactly what we're seeing," Blanco said.She tells me she's noticed a change in how and where those arrests have happened in recent months in Palm Beach County."So they're not just taking the driver in the vehicle; they're taking the passengers as well," Blanco said."When (people) called to report crimes, (deputies) have been arresting them because of their — due to their immigration status," Blanco said.I asked her if the person who called to report the crime gets arrested, and she confirmed that they do.I asked Blanco whether she worries about the impact that will have on crime overall in Lake Worth."Crime has been heavily under-reported in Lake Worth and I know that because PBSO has asked us for help in ... giving a sense of security for the people to report crimes," Blanco said. "We said, well, respectfully, we don't trust you, and so how would we tell the people that they could trust you?" entry.article_text: Thousands of Port St. Lucie residents can put away their pots after city officials lifted a precautionary boil water notice Saturday afternoon. The City of Port St. Lucie announced the all-clear at 3:15 p.m. Saturday after water quality tests confirmed the water was safe to drink. The notice affected approximately 21,000 customers in Tradition and areas west of Interstate 95 following a water main break Tuesday near Glades Cut Off Road. See also: A helping of hope: 600 turkeys bring Thanksgiving cheer to South Florida families Residents in the following communities no longer need to boil their water: Tradition Western Grove Riverland Wilson Grove Southern Grove Copper Creek Wylder Verano The affected area stretched west of I-95 south to Becker Road, including communities along Glades Cut Off Road. According to city officials, the break occurred when a contractor working on a construction project unrelated to the city damaged a 36-inch water main. City crews responded immediately and completed repairs within hours. Flushing and required water quality testing followed. After tests confirmed the water was safe, officials lifted the precautionary notice. The city thanked the roughly 21,000 affected customers for their patience throughout the disruption.

entry.title: Memorial honors two Indian River County deputies killed in line of duty - Sebastian Daily
entry.summary: Memorial honors two Indian River County deputies killed in line of duty    Sebastian Daily
entry.article_text: Home Community News in Sebastian, Florida Memorial honors two Indian River County deputies killed in line of duty by Tina Hodges Nov 23, 2026 / 8:23 AM A A A A Reset The stone monument carries the names of Sgt. Terri Sweeting-Mashkow and Cpl. Richard Raczkoski (Indian River County Sheriff's Office) Share on Twitter Share via Email VERO BEACH — Bagpipes and taps filled the air Saturday as the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office unveiled a new memorial outside its administration complex honoring two deputies killed in the line of duty nearly 40 years apart. The stone monument, a roughly 10-foot obelisk, carries the names of Sgt. Terri Sweeting-Mashkow and Cpl. The ceremony fell exactly one year after Sweeting-Mashkow, 47, was fatally shot while serving an eviction notice at a home in the Bermuda Club community. Raczkoski, 29, was killed Sept. 23, 1986, after responding to a call at a convenience store on State Road 60 west of Vero Beach. Hundreds of family members, fellow officers and community members gathered for the unveiling, which included a three-volley salute, “Amazing Grace,” a rose tribute and the last radio call for Sweeting-Mashkow. “On this one-year anniversary of the death of Terri Sweeting-Mashkow, we dedicate this memorial to both her and Corporal Richard Raczkoski, who was killed in the line of duty 40 years ago,” Sheriff Eric Flowers told Sebastian Daily . “By placing the memorial at the front of our new administration building before we take occupancy, we ensure that every employee, every visitor, and future generations will always know the names and memory of our fallen heroes.” He added that he hopes the agency never has to add another name. Sweeting-Mashkow had served more than 25 years with the sheriff’s office, much of it in patrol before she moved to the civil process unit. She was one of three deputies at the Bermuda Club residence when Michael Halberstam, 37, opened fire, authorities said. Deputy Florentino Arizpe was shot in the shoulder. Locksmith David Long, who was there to assist with the eviction, was critically wounded and later died. Deputies returned fire; Halberstam died the following day. Her death was the second line-of-duty killing in the roughly 100-year history of the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office. He answered a 911 hang-up from a phone booth outside a Zippy Mart. During the encounter, a handgun fell from William Reaves’ clothing. After a short struggle, Reaves shot Raczkoski four times in the back as the deputy tried to run. Reaves was convicted of first-degree murder, sentenced to death, and executed Oct. 20, 2026. The memorial stands outside the new administration building on the sheriff’s campus at 4055 41st Ave. The building is expected to open next spring. entry.title: West Boca Raton neighbors clean up after EF-1 tornado damages homes, cars
entry.summary: An EF-1 tornado that swept through southern Palm Beach County over the weekend left residents in the Boca Gardens community of west Boca Raton cleaning up downed trees and damaged property, including a car crushed by a massive tree. Two days after the tornado, cleanup crews were still working through Boca Gardens, where residents described powerful winds, widespread debris and the shock of seeing the damage once the storm had passed. WATCH: West Boca Raton neighbors clean up EF-1 tornado damage West Boca Raton neighbors clean up after EF-1 tornado leaves trail of damage Boca Gardens residents describe tornado's impact Greg Ciaro and Angela Cairo live yards from where a large tree came down. The couple told WPTV they realized afterward how much worse the damage could have been. 'The wind just came down, really strong,' Greg said. 'Total devastation. I mean, we walked out afterward, and you're just in shock,' Angela said. The family said the tree's proximity to their home made clear how narrowly they avoided more serious damage. 'I mean, if you think about it, it's literally right there. We're right here. So any shift this way easily could've been much, much worse,' he said. Tree crushes neighbor's car Down the road, resident Alvaro Villa Correa is dealing with the loss of his vehicle after a tree came crashing down on it. 'The car is a total loss. It's too badly damaged,' Villa Correa told WPTV. 'The roof, the hood, the trunk, there's major damage.' Cleanup crews continued cutting and removing downed trees Monday. Crews told WPTV the cleanup is expected to be a lengthy process. How El Nio can influence South Florida weather The tornado is one of several tornado events WPTV has reported across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast in recent years. WPTV First Alert Meteorologist Skylar Spinler said El Nio can influence local weather patterns because Pacific Ocean temperatures affect the position and strength of the subtropical jet stream. 'During El Nio winters, the subtropical jet stream typically strengthens and shifts further south, so think of this jet stream as a highway for storm systems,' Spinler said. Neighbors thankful after close call For residents continuing to clean up in Boca Gardens, the destruction is also a reminder of what did not happen. 'We were blessed. 100% we were blessed,' Angela told WPTV. With Thanksgiving approaching, she said her family has an added reason to be grateful. Crews told WPTV the cleanup is expected to be a lengthy process.How El Niño can influence South Florida weatherThe tornado is one of several tornado events WPTV has reported across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast in recent years.WPTV First Alert Meteorologist Skylar Spinler said El Niño can influence local weather patterns because Pacific Ocean temperatures affect the position and strength of the subtropical jet stream."During El Niño winters, the subtropical jet stream typically strengthens and shifts further south, so think of this jet stream as a highway for storm systems," Spinler said.Neighbors thankful after close callFor residents continuing to clean up in Boca Gardens, the destruction is also a reminder of what did not happen."We were blessed. 100% we were blessed," Angela told WPTV.With Thanksgiving approaching, she said her family has an added reason to be grateful."And we've got a lot to be thankful for on Thanksgiving because it could've been so much worse," Angela said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Riviera Beach launches 'Rebuild Lone Pine Together' to help families recover from historic flooding
entry.summary: Three weeks after historic flooding damaged and destroyed homes in Riviera Beach's Lone Pine community, residents are still gutting houses, searching for materials and relying on volunteers as they try to rebuild. Now, Mayor Douglas Lawson says the city is launching Rebuild Lone Pine Together, a community-driven initiative aimed at getting money, manpower and other resources to families who need help immediately. WPTV reporter Michael Hoffman was in Lone Pine the night of the flooding and returned to the neighborhood weeks later. WATCH: Riviera Beach launches effort to rebuild Lone Pine Riviera Beach launches 'Rebuild Lone Pine Together' to help families recover from historic flooding The water is gone, but signs of the destruction remain throughout the community. Dumpsters line streets outside gutted homes as families work to rebuild their lives heading into the holiday season. Volunteers step in to help rebuild homes Inside one of those damaged homes, Hoffman met Edward Carr. Carr doesn't live in Lone Pine. He answered a call for volunteers after historic rainfall devastated the neighborhood. 'They said they needed some drywall, like replaced because they had flooding,' Carr said. 'So as you can see, I started pulling off the baseboards.' The family living in the home invited WPTV inside but asked to remain anonymous. That's also where Hoffman met Denise Smith, another Lone Pine resident. 'We need a lot of hands because many hands make light work,' Smith said. 'It's what my grandmother used to say.' Smith's own home down the street was destroyed by the flooding. She showed WPTV images of the damage. Despite being displaced herself, she was helping someone else rebuild. For Smith and Carr, two needs stand out across Lone Pine: volunteers and building materials. 'Right now is the time for Riviera Beach to come together' 'Right now is the time for Riviera Beach to come together as one community,' Lawson said. Hoffman walked through Lone Pine with Lawson as they discussed what comes next for families who cannot afford to wait. Lawson said the city is working to bring together $2 million in available funding. But he also acknowledged that accessing money can involve bureaucratic hurdles, while residents need help now. That's where Rebuild Lone Pine Together comes in. 'It's really driven and led by the community,' Lawson said. 'It's focused on community advocates, leaders, nonprofits to come together with the resources, the funding, the dollars, the manpower.'

entry.title: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse launches Luminary Nights as new holiday tradition
entry.summary: A new holiday tradition is taking root at the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, where Luminary Nights will bring holiday lights, nighttime lighthouse climbs, local music and shopping to the historic waterfront property in December. The limited event is scheduled for Dec. 11, 12, 18, and 19. Organizers say they are starting small this year with hopes of growing Luminary Nights into an annual family tradition in northern Palm Beach County. 'We really hope to make this a new family-friendly holiday tradition here in North County,' Executive Director Katrina Heller said. A Banyan tree (ficus) that dances to music One of the most visual additions will be the Lighthouse's illuminated Banyan tree. Organizers have nicknamed it the 'Dancing Tree' because its lights have been synchronized to music. 'We have lit it up and timed it to music, so we're calling it our dancing tree, and we'll have a new program every half hour,' Heller said. Luminary Nights will also feature nighttime lighthouse climbs, holiday shopping, live music and a Kids Zone for families. Lighthouse climbs are limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis. Children must be at least 48 inches tall to climb. Tickets are $30 for adults and $20 for children. A family ticket for two adults and two children is $75. Keeping the holiday celebration local Event Manager Simone Incendy said organizers are intentionally incorporating local businesses and musicians into Luminary Nights. The Vendor Village will feature local artists and small businesses, including vendors whose products are carried in the Lighthouse gift shop. Incendy said area high school bands and community bands will also be among the performers. The approach connects the new celebration to the community surrounding the landmark while giving small businesses and local performers another place to reach visitors during the holiday season. Proceeds from the event will go toward preserving the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, its history and its educational programming, according to event information provided by organizers. A new view of the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse The holiday celebration isn't the only new attraction visitors will find at the Lighthouse. Heller said a shoreline restoration project is wrapping up with a grand opening scheduled for Dec. 3 at 1 p.m. The work includes a new seawall and a boardwalk stretching more than 800 feet around the point where the Loxahatchee River and Indian River meet. entry.title: Treasure Coast counties prepare for flooding as heavy rain and gusty winds move in - WPEC
entry.summary: Treasure Coast counties prepare for flooding as heavy rain and gusty winds move in    WPEC
entry.article_text: The Treasure Coast is bracing for a soggy stretch as counties prepare for possible flooding from heavy rain. Indian River County The Indian River County Emergency Operations Center remains at Level 2, or partial activation, because of ongoing flooding and the potential for more heavy rain. Emergency services, human services and infrastructure partners are coordinating response and recovery efforts. The county urges residents to avoid flooded roads and floodwaters, watch for rising water in low-lying areas and monitor weather conditions and official updates. Residents with flood-related questions or information can call the Emergency Information Center at 772-226-4000 during operating hours. Due to the heavy rain and gusty winds, solid waste services may be disrupted. Waste Management curbside collections may be delayed, and residents should not put carts in the street if it is flooded. See also: Florida deputies rescue 2-year-old girl found in pond near apartment complex Waste Management collects recycling in blue carts countywide. It collects garbage, yard waste and bulk waste in unincorporated Indian River County, Fellsmere, Sebastian and Indian River Shores. Residents in other cities and towns should check with their local governments for service updates. The county recommends putting carts out by 6 a.m. on collection day, closing lids, bagging garbage, and avoiding overfilled carts. Cardboard should be flattened and placed inside recycling carts, and yard waste should stay inside yard waste carts. Residents should bring carts back in as soon as possible after collection. The landfill and all five Customer Convenience Centers may close early or remain closed if conditions become unsafe. The east-central Florida coast faces a Slight Risk, or Level 2 out of 4, for excessive rainfall. Localized flooding is possible, especially along the coast, and some areas could receive 4 inches or more of rain. Martin County Martin County officials expect 3 to 6 inches of rain, with localized amounts of 8 to 12 inches, beginning Tuesday afternoon and continuing through Nov. 20. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office says it is working with the county’s emergency operations center to monitor rainfall and identify roads that could become difficult to pass. The sheriff’s office plans to deploy high-water rescue vehicles in flood-prone areas. Having the vehicles nearby could help deputies reach residents who need assistance and motorists who become stranded, the office said. The sheriff’s office advises residents to turn around if water covers the road. Standing water may be deeper than it appears and can hide damage. If a regular route is flooded, drivers should take another route or wait somewhere safe. Residents should never drive around barricades or enter flooded areas to see how high the water is. Martin County Fire Rescue also advises residents to be prepared to evacuate if flooding threatens their homes or neighborhoods and to have an emergency kit ready for household members and pets. The Community Information Center will be open to provide flood-related information. Okeechobee County Okeechobee County is also preparing for severe flooding. The Okeechobee County Sheriff’s Office says its emergency operations center will remain active as staff coordinate response and recovery efforts from past flooding. Sandbags are available at Okeechobee County Public Works, 804 Northwest Second St. St. Lucie County The St. Lucie County Public Safety Department is monitoring the forecast and reminding residents to secure loose items that could be damaged by wind. Gusty northeast winds of 25 to 30 mph are forecast Tuesday and Wednesday, with gusts of 35 to 40 mph along the coast. Residents should secure tarps, patio furniture and other unsecured items. A rip current advisory remains in effect for St. Lucie County beaches. Strong onshore winds can create dangerous rip currents and rough surf. The St. Lucie County Fire District says its firefighters, paramedics and telecommunicators are prepared to respond as the area faces more heavy rain and recovers from recent flooding. The district has high-water vehicles and a rescue boat available to assist during flood-related emergencies. Free sand is available while supplies last at two self-service locations: County Fairgrounds: 5601 W. Midway Road, Fort Pierce, in the west parking lot Lawnwood Stadium: 2000 Virginia Ave., Fort Pierce Residents should bring their own bags, shovel and other supplies. Residents can use Community Connect to share household information that could help firefighters prepare for an emergency. The county has extended the deadline to Nov. 30 for residents to report flood damage through an online survey. The information will help document flooding across the community and inform recovery efforts. The survey is open to property owners and tenants throughout St. Lucie County, including Fort Pierce, Port St. Lucie, St. Lucie Village and unincorporated areas. It asks where flooding occurred, how buildings were affected and what impacts residents and businesses experienced. Residents can complete the flood damage survey by Nov. 30. Officials urge residents across the region to avoid flooded roads and keep roadways clear for emergency responders. If you encounter flooding, turn around and find a safe alternate route.

entry.title: 4 men taken into custody after overnight burglary, manhunt in Martin County
entry.summary: Four men were taken into custody following an overnight burglary and manhunt in Palm City, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. The sheriff's office said it has confirmed at least one burglary in the Evergreen Club community. Deputies tracked four men who were wearing masks and gloves during the night before taking all four into custody, according to the agency. The sheriff's office said the men are from Jacksonville. Authorities are now asking Palm City residents, particularly those who live in the Evergreen Club, to check their vehicles and the outside of their homes for any signs of a break-in or missing property. Anyone who discovers property missing or believes someone tried to break into their home or vehicle is asked to contact the Martin County Sheriffs Office at 772-220-7060. The names of the suspects have not been released. The sheriff's office said more information about the overnight manhunt is expected to be released later Tuesday.

entry.title: Man arrested after 19-year-old woman escapes attempted sexual assault in Boca Raton, police say
entry.summary: A 19-year-old woman escaped with minor injuries after police say a man armed with a knife forced her into a wooded area along Boca Ratons El Rio Trail and attempted to sexually assault her Monday morning. Boca Raton police said 36-year-old LaPaul Jackson was arrested a short time later aboard a public bus as he allegedly tried to leave the area. Officers responded shortly after 11:30 a.m. to a report of an assault along the El Rio Trail, just north of Spanish River Boulevard. According to police, the woman was walking along the trail when a man she did not know approached her from behind with a knife. Investigators said he forced her into a nearby wooded area where a small camp had been set up. Police said the man attempted to sexually assault the woman and committed additional lewd acts before she was able to escape and run back toward the trail. Another person then called police. The woman suffered minor injuries and gave officers a detailed description of the suspect, police said. Officers established a perimeter and worked with the woman to track her cellphone, which police said the suspect had taken. Real-time location information showed the phone was moving, leading investigators to believe the suspect had boarded a public bus. Officers stopped the bus near North Federal Highway and Northeast 20th Street. Police said they identified Jackson aboard the bus and recovered the woman's cellphone. Jackson was arrested on charges of armed kidnapping, armed robbery and attempted sexual battery. Police said additional charges are pending. He was later taken to the Palm Beach County Jail. The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with information is asked to contact Boca Raton police Detective Gannon at 561-620-6073.

entry.title: U2 announces 2027 stadium tour with North American kickoff at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami
entry.summary: U2 is heading back to stadiums, and the rock band's newly announced North American tour will begin in Miami. Live Nation announced U2's Carnaval De Luz presents: The Greatest Show On Earth World Tour 2027 will kick off its North American leg at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens on Aug. 13, 2027. The tour will feature Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton and Larry Mullen Jr. and include 15 stadium shows across the United States and Canada. The announcement comes as U2 promotes its 16th studio album, 'Carnaval De Luz,' which was released Nov. 13. The 12-track album is the band's first new release in nine years. The North American dates follow previously announced shows in Latin America and Europe. According to Live Nation, initial concerts in Mexico City, So Paulo and Buenos Aires sold out, prompting additional dates. The 2027 tour will mark U2's first stadium outing since The Joshua Tree Tour concluded in Mumbai in December 2019. Live Nation said that tour was seen by nearly 3 million fans worldwide. U2's most recent major live production was its 40-show residency at Sphere in Las Vegas. Fans will have several opportunities to get tickets before the general sale. The U2.com Subscriber Presale begins Monday, Nov. 30, at 10 a.m. Visa cardholders will have access to a separate presale Wednesday, Dec. 2, from 10 a.m. until 10 p.m., while supplies last. An artist presale begins Thursday, Dec. 3, at 10 a.m. local time. Fans must register by Sunday, Nov. 29, at 9 p.m. ET to participate. No presale code is required because access will be linked to the fan's account. Remaining tickets will go on sale to the general public Friday, Dec. 4, at 10 a.m. through U2.com .

entry.title: Atlantic High School students, Delray Beach police deliver Thanksgiving meals to families in need
entry.summary: Thanksgiving came with a little extra help for families in Delray Beach as local high school students teamed up with police officers to make sure they had a holiday meal on the table. Students from Atlantic High Schools Criminal Justice Academy partnered with the Delray Beach Police Department to deliver more than a dozen full Thanksgiving meals to families in need across the city. WATCH: Atlantic High School students, Delray Beach police deliver Thanksgiving meals to families in need Students give away Thanksgiving meals For the students, the annual effort is about more than dropping off food. Its an opportunity to learn what it means to serve the community beyond the classroom. It teaches you to be less selfish and care more about what is going on around you and how you can help, student Alexis Felicetta said. The students went door to door alongside Delray Beach police officers, personally delivering the meals and meeting the families receiving them. We are helping families, and seeing them smile when they open the door makes me happy, student Micaja Paul Joseph said. The Thanksgiving meal giveaway has become a tradition for the Criminal Justice Academy and Delray Beach police, continuing for more than decade. Major Gary Ferreri with the Delray Beach Police Department said the experience also gives students perspective on hardships other people in their community may be facing. Some of the kids come from tough situations. They get to see that even as bad as they have it, there are others that have it tougher sometimes. For one family, the delivery meant being able to have a Thanksgiving turkey without worrying about how to pay for it. We didn't really have money to buy a turkey for Thanksgiving, a family member said. For me, it's happy because I get to spend more time with my family. For the students, police officers and families taking part, the tradition is proving a little help can go a long way.

entry.title: Top American golf courses rated, where do Florida courses rank?
entry.summary: What is the best golf course in America? Golf.com broke down the top 100 courses, they call it a Bucket List for American Golf. (link ). So, how do they determine the list? Its a democratic vote with the panelists. Golf.com said each panelist gets a ballot with hundreds of courses. Beside the list of courses are 11 groupings. If a panelist considers a course to be among the top three in the U.S., they tick the first column. If they believe the course to be among Nos. 4-10, they check that column, followed by 11-25 and so on. They even have a column for remove.  The organization is also careful with panelist selections to include a variety of input and to avoid anyone with ties to any of the courses. Research shows golf is experiencing a resurgence as a hobby. The National Golf Foundation reports 30.6 million Americans play golf, thats up 1.7 million from the previous year and a new record in playing. Did any Florida courses make the list? Course: TPC Sawgrass (Players Stadium) , Ponte Vedra Beach Rank: 53 Built: 1981 Designer : Pete Dye Course : Seminole , Juno Beach Rank: 17 Built: 1926 Designer: Donald Ross

entry.title: IRC sheriff renews push for unified 911 dispatch as Vero Beach weighs Amendment 3 cuts - cw34.com
entry.summary: IRC sheriff renews push for unified 911 dispatch as Vero Beach weighs Amendment 3 cuts    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers asked the Vero Beach City Council on Tuesday to take another look at merging emergency dispatch. He pitched it as a way to save money as the city prepares for revenue losses under Amendment 3 . Flowers said he first brought the idea to the council about two years ago. He said Brevard County has since moved to a unified dispatch system, and he told council members his offer still stands. "I'm not asking for anything specific today. I just want to make sure that it's known that it is my desire that we go to a unified dispatch system," Flowers said. He asked that it be considered "as a potential cost savings" as the city makes what he called "difficult decisions" under Amendment 3. Florida voters approved a ballot initiative that will slash non-school property taxes despite a campaign by local officials warning it would gut funding for public safety and other services. It will increase the homestead exemption from about $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Council member Tracey Zudans asked city staff to put numbers on the idea. "I'd love to see some numbers attached to it, not just response time numbers, but also some dollar numbers so that we can share that with our taxpayers as well," Zudans said. "I'd be happy to have my staff work with you guys," Flowers said. Vice Mayor John Cotugno asked whether the dispatch center would be a county function or run by the sheriff's office. Flowers said the county technically runs dispatch, but most dispatchers work for his agency. "I have the bulk of dispatchers that work for me at the sheriff's office, so I can only offer it from my side," Flowers said. "You would have to ask the county if they were interested in maybe doing it differently." He added that the sheriff's office and the county are still discussing how Amendment 3 will affect their relationship. See also: 22-year-old West Palm Beach motorcyclist struck, killed by SUV in Loxahatchee That relationship has been strained before. In July 2025 a budget debate erupted during an Indian River County Commission meeting, prompting the board to call a 15-minute recess after tensions flared between commissioners and Flowers. Flowers was requesting $93.5 million that year, while the county recommended a budget closer to $83.5 million. Commissioners ultimately voted to raise the sheriff's budget by $6.8 million, far less than he requested. Flowers later sued the commission , which then held a special meeting over the sheriff's budget. "This is a very deep issue," Flowers said. "If we do it as a county, if we do it under me, either way, I'm just trying to get all of our dispatchers in the same room together." Council members took no action on the proposal.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to nearly 4 years in $260K AI cryptocurrency fraud scheme
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie man has been sentenced to nearly four years in federal prison for using artificial intelligence to impersonate a popular online streamer as part of a cryptocurrency fraud scheme that authorities say cost victims about $260,000. David Anthony Sanchez, 36, was sentenced to 47 months in federal prison after pleading guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida. Federal prosecutors said Sanchez, who also went by 'Dave the Jewler,' 'Rueben Alexis De Jesus Santana' and other aliases, impersonated online streamer N3ON to convince organizers of a cryptocurrency memecoin project that the streamer had agreed to endorse and participate in it. According to court records, Sanchez created online accounts designed to look as though they belonged to N3ON and communicated with the project's organizers while posing as both the streamer and his representative. Prosecutors said Sanchez also executed agreements using N3ON's identity and sent organizers an AI-generated voice recording that mimicked the streamer's voice to falsely confirm his participation. Believing the representations were legitimate, the victims transferred approximately $260,000 in cryptocurrency to accounts controlled by Sanchez, according to prosecutors. Authorities said Sanchez later converted a substantial portion of the cryptocurrency into U.S. dollars through transactions designed to conceal the source and ownership of the money. Prosecutors said he used the proceeds for his personal benefit. 'Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm,' Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas said in the release. She said Sanchez exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate victims' trust and take their money. In addition to his 47-month prison sentence, Sanchez was ordered to pay restitution to the victims. The amount of restitution was not specified in the release. The FBI's Miami Field Office investigated the case.

'SPECTRA is our not-for-profit arm of the Housing Authority,' Chief Financial Officer Tad Fuller said. 'The Housing Authority, of course, houses individuals and families within our county. entry.title: Florida commissioner's son shot and killed while camping
entry.summary: The 19-year-old son of a Florida county commissioner was shot and killed while camping in Santa Rosa County on Sunday. Carey Washington Vinson, a history major at Florida State University, was the son of Joe Vinson, who was recently elected to the Escambia County Commission. The Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office said investigators are working to identify those involved in Carey's death and determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting. No arrests have been announced. In an emotional Facebook post Tuesday, Joe Vinson remembered his son, whom the family affectionately called 'Wash,' and pushed back against suggestions that his death was an accident. 'This was not a freak hunting accident not someone firing carelessly in the dark,' Vinson wrote. 'It was not a 'stray bullet' that killed our Wash.' According to Vinson, the family understands that someone stood on the opposite bank of the river and pointed a gun toward the occupied sandbar campground. He said the shooters were close enough to see the campfire and hear people talking. 'They fired shot after shot with malicious intent,' Vinson wrote, alleging that the shooters fired another round after campers screamed for them to stop, then laughed as they drove away. Those details reflect the family's understanding of the shooting. The sheriff's office has not publicly confirmed that account in the statement provided. Vinson remembered his son as a thoughtful, outgoing young man who loved history, music and adventure. Carey was an excellent debater, played piano and guitar, and had recently been accepted into a summer study-abroad program in Valencia. 'Most of all, he had a tender and loving heart for his friends and family, for his girlfriend, for animals, for the marginalized,' Vinson wrote. 'He was quick to laugh and easy to love.' 'I can't believe I'll never feel his hugs again, or hear him bickering with his siblings,' his father wrote. 'I can't believe any of this.' The Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office is asking anyone who witnessed suspicious activity near Deaton Bridge Road and Boat Ramp Road, or who has information that could help identify those involved, to contact investigators. Anyone with information can call the sheriff's office at 850-983-1190, Option 1. Anonymous tips can also be submitted to Santa Rosa Crime Stoppers at 850-437-STOP (7867) or through the P3 Tips mobile app. 'I know it won't bring back Wash, but I would sleep better knowing they can't hurt anyone else,' Vinson wrote.

entry.title: Neighbors plead for help as repeated flooding threatens their Indian River County homes
entry.summary: People across South Florida and the Treasure Coast are bracing for yet another round of heavy rain , and one Indian River County community is pleading for help after battling repeated flooding this month. Joe Waters documented his frustration Saturday evening, recording on his phone in front of his mobile home in the Heritage Plantation mobile home park near Vero Beach as a car drove through floodwaters that almost covered its headlights. Waters said the wake caused by passing vehicles crashed into the bricks that protect the undercarriage of his home, toppling them. 'The water came up probably about thigh high,' Waters said. 'Came up into the driveway, went into the house.' Waters and his wife were able to clean their home, but he said his car is still in the shop with $4,600 worth of damage, waiting on approval from the insurance company. When we showed up at Heritage Plantation Tuesday afternoon, a crowd of neighbors gathered fed up after battling multiple floods just this month. Dawn Carboni, the HOA president, told me she wants to be a voice for her neighbors, especially those who can't speak up. 'They just want to feel safe in their homes,' she said. The flooding has created dangerous conditions for emergency responders, Carboni said. 'We had a gentleman who needed EMS to come out, and they could not get to his home, so they had to park out on 82nd (Avenue), and then a large fire truck had to get to the home,' Carboni said. With more heavy rain in the forecast, Carboni said residents are frightened. 'People are afraid. It's horrible living in fear when you don't know if it's going to rain and you're going to be able to leave your home the next day.' She wants to spread awareness about what her community is going through. 'We need help, and we're asking for help,' Carboni said. entry.title: Top American golf courses rated, where do Florida courses rank?
entry.summary: What is the best golf course in America? Golf.com broke down the top 100 courses, which they call a 'Top 100 Courses in the U.S. for 2026-27: The ultimate bucket list for American golf' . So, how do they determine the list? It's a democratic vote with the panelists. Golf.com said each panelist gets a ballot with hundreds of courses. Beside the list of courses are 11 groupings. If a panelist considers a course to be among the top three in the U.S., they tick the first column. If they believe the course to be among Nos. 4-10, they check that column, followed by 11-25 and so on. They even have a column for remove.  The organization is also careful with panelist selections to include a variety of input and to avoid anyone with ties to any of the courses. Research shows golf is experiencing a resurgence as a hobby. The National Golf Foundation reports that 30.6 million Americans play golf, that's up 1.7 million from the previous year and a new record. Did any Florida courses make the list? Course: TPC Sawgrass (Players Stadium) , Ponte Vedra Beach Rank: 53 Built: 1981 Designer : Pete Dye Course : Seminole , Juno Beach Rank: 17 Built: 1926 Designer: Donald Ross

entry.title: IRC sheriff renews push for unified 911 dispatch as Vero Beach weighs Amendment 3 cuts - cw34.com
entry.summary: IRC sheriff renews push for unified 911 dispatch as Vero Beach weighs Amendment 3 cuts    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers asked the Vero Beach City Council on Tuesday to take another look at merging emergency dispatch. He pitched it as a way to save money as the city prepares for revenue losses under Amendment 3 . Flowers said he first brought the idea to the council about two years ago. He said Brevard County has since moved to a unified dispatch system, and he told council members his offer still stands. "I'm not asking for anything specific today. I just want to make sure that it's known that it is my desire that we go to a unified dispatch system," Flowers said. He asked that it be considered "as a potential cost savings" as the city makes what he called "difficult decisions" under Amendment 3. Florida voters approved a ballot initiative that will slash non-school property taxes despite a campaign by local officials warning it would gut funding for public safety and other services. It will increase the homestead exemption from about $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Council member Tracey Zudans asked city staff to put numbers on the idea. "I'd love to see some numbers attached to it, not just response time numbers, but also some dollar numbers so that we can share that with our taxpayers as well," Zudans said. "I'd be happy to have my staff work with you guys," Flowers said. Vice Mayor John Cotugno asked whether the dispatch center would be a county function or run by the sheriff's office. Flowers said the county technically runs dispatch, but most dispatchers work for his agency. "I have the bulk of dispatchers that work for me at the sheriff's office, so I can only offer it from my side," Flowers said. "You would have to ask the county if they were interested in maybe doing it differently." He added that the sheriff's office and the county are still discussing how Amendment 3 will affect their relationship. See also: 22-year-old West Palm Beach motorcyclist struck, killed by SUV in Loxahatchee That relationship has been strained before. In July 2025 a budget debate erupted during an Indian River County Commission meeting, prompting the board to call a 15-minute recess after tensions flared between commissioners and Flowers. Flowers was requesting $93.5 million that year, while the county recommended a budget closer to $83.5 million. Commissioners ultimately voted to raise the sheriff's budget by $6.8 million, far less than he requested. Flowers later sued the commission , which then held a special meeting over the sheriff's budget. "This is a very deep issue," Flowers said. "If we do it as a county, if we do it under me, either way, I'm just trying to get all of our dispatchers in the same room together." Council members took no action on the proposal.

entry.title: 4 men arrested after attempted home invasion at Martin County’s Evergreen Club - WPEC
entry.summary: 4 men arrested after attempted home invasion at Martin County’s Evergreen Club    WPEC
entry.article_text: A homeowner in Palm City helped foil an attempted home invasion that occurred at the Evergreen Club. The Martin County Sheriff's Office says on Tuesday morning a homeowner on SW Bimini Circle heard a noise outside of their home, leading them to call 911 and interrupting the home invasion. When deputies arrived at the scene, the four suspects, three men and a teenager from Jacksonville, scattered into the neighborhood. The sheriff's office says deputies set up a perimeter around the neighborhood with help from its aviation team, K-9 unit, and the Stuart Police Department. K9's were able to track down all four suspects hiding in separate locations throughout the community. The sheriff's office says at least one of the suspects was armed. Further investigation revealed that the suspects parked along the canal and walked into the neighborhood to target the home. The sheriff's office says during the apprehension they uncovered masks, a firearm and gloves. The suspects were identified as: Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr, 21 Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews, 21 Cameron Elijah Mapson, 21 Teenage boy, 16 All four were charged with an attempted home invasion and were taken to the Martin County Jail. Wise faces an additional charge of grand theft and possession of a firearm. See also: Boca Raton police arrest man after reported assault on El Rio Trail The agency is asking Palm City residents to check their homes and vehicles for missing property or signs of a break-in. Anyone who finds anything missing should call the sheriff’s office at 772-220-7060. This is a developing news story.

entry.title: Nearly 1.8 million chickens to be depopulated after bird flu detected at Okeechobee County facility
entry.summary: Nearly 1.8 million chickens will be depopulated after highly pathogenic avian influenza, commonly known as bird flu, was detected at a Cal-Maine Foods facility in Okeechobee County. Cal-Maine Foods announced Nov. 18 that the facility tested positive for highly pathogenic avian influenza, or HPAI. The company said the outbreak will lead to the depopulation of approximately 1.4 million laying hens and 360,000 pullets, representing about 2.7% of the company's total flock. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Bird flu detected at Okeechobee County poultry facility Production at the Okeechobee County facility has temporarily stopped while Cal-Maine follows protocols established by the U.S. Department of Agriculture. The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services has established a quarantine area following the detection, according to St. Lucie County government. The poultry quarantine extends from Okeechobee County into a rural portion of western St. Lucie County north of State Road 70 near the county line. People who own or care for poultry within the affected area are being advised to review the state's quarantine restrictions, which include limits on moving poultry and poultry products without FDACS authorization. Residents can check whether they are within the affected area using the state's interactive quarantine map. Cal-Maine said it is coordinating production and distribution among its other facilities in an effort to maintain its egg supply and minimize disruptions for customers. The company also said it maintains biosecurity programs at its facilities but noted that no farm is immune to HPAI. The virus remains present among wild birds, and the risk of outbreaks can increase during bird migration seasons. Health officials say the detection does not mean consumers should stop eating eggs. According to information provided by the company, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention considers the health risk from HPAI viruses to the general U.S. public to be low. The USDA also says HPAI is not transmitted through properly handled and cooked eggs. Cal-Maine said there is no known HPAI risk associated with eggs currently on the market and that no eggs have been recalled because of the outbreak. Cal-Maine said it is working with federal, state and local officials as it responds to the outbreak and works to reduce the risk of additional infections. entry.title: Panthers ready for Ottawa Senators and potential return of Barkov, Marchand
entry.summary: The Florida Panthers held practice at Baptist Health Iceplex in Fort Lauderdale Tuesday morning. Anticipation is building for the Wednesday night matchup against the Ottawa Senators at Amerant Bank Arena. Watch report from Mike Trim: Panthers ready for Ottawa Senators and potential return of Barkov, Marchand Perhaps the largest source of that anticipation is the potential return of two Panther superstars: Captain Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand. While not confirming the two stars would be inserted back into the lineup Wednesday, head coach Paul Maurice addressed the media after practice and said, There's a possibility it's both. After missing all of last season to a right knee injury , Barkov returned to the Panthers lineup this season only to injure his left knee in the second game. Marchand was injured the following game. Neither has played since their injuries. Speaking about Barkov, Maurice said, I mean, he's one of the best players in the world, and we just haven't had him here for a year and a half. Big trades around the league. I think we made the biggest one. We got Barkov for nothing. Panthers defenseman Niko Mikkola talked about the boost Barkov would give the team. Oh, it's huge. He's the face of the team, leader, and our most important player, so it's, it's huge. This will be Panthers forward Brady Tkachuks first time facing his old team here in Florida. Tkachuk played eight seasons in Ottawa, serving as captain the last five. WPTV Florida Panthers anchor Mike Trim connected with Tkachuk after practice with other members of the media. This new chapter has been awesome and to have this game at home, it's still going to be different, but I'm really excited about doing it in front of our home fans. A special promotion for Wednesday nights game will have a Thanksgiving theme. The first 10,000 fans into the arena will receive a Panthers oven mitt. Puck drop is set for 7 p.m. Wednesday. The game will be shown on WPTV and The Spot South Florida.

entry.article_text: A major multi-vehicle crash shut down all northbound lanes of Florida's Turnpike in Martin County on Tuesday afternoon, causing traffic disruptions for drivers. All northbound lanes were blocked, and the incident was classified as major. According to Florida 511, the crash is before mile marker 126 and mile marker 130. According to FHP, all northbound lanes reopened at 1:56 p.m. As of 3 p.m. the right shoulder is still blocked, according to Florida 511. The crash involved a medium-duty truck hauling a trailer loaded with pallets of mulch and a sport utility vehicle. Both vehicles were traveling northbound when the truck jackknifed and struck the wall and the SUV. Four individuals were transported to Florida Coast Medical Center, and one was transported to Martin Memorial South. Photos from the scene show multiple emergency vehicles and large trucks at the scene. Cars were also seen on the grass shoulder. The incident is classified as major. According to the Florida Highway Patrol , injuries are associated with the incident. entry.title: Port St. Lucie man gets 47 months in federal prison for $260K N3ON deepfake cryptoscam - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie man gets 47 months in federal prison for $260K N3ON deepfake cryptoscam    WPEC
entry.article_text: A fake online persona, an AI-generated voice and a $260,000 cryptocurrency payday. Federal prosecutors say a Port St. Lucie man used all three to pull off an elaborate fraud scheme involving a popular internet streamer. 36,-year-old David Anthony Sanchez, also known as "Dave the Jewler," was sentenced to 47 months in federal prison Tuesday after pleading guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida . The scheme centered on popular online streamer N3ON , whose identity Sanchez hijacked to convince organizers of a cryptocurrency project that the internet personality was backing their investment. According to federal court records, Sanchez created fake online accounts posing as N3ON and his representative, communicating directly with organizers of a cryptocurrency "memecoin" project . But the impersonation went beyond fake profiles. Prosecutors said Sanchez used artificial intelligence to generate an audio recording mimicking N3ON's voice, falsely confirming the streamer's involvement in the project. Sanchez also signed agreements using N3ON's identity, further convincing organizers that the endorsement was legitimate. See also: Riviera Beach mayor calls for volunteers, supplies to aid Lone Pine Estates flood recovery The deception worked. Believing they had secured the streamer's participation, the victims transferred approximately $260,000 in cryptocurrency to accounts controlled by Sanchez, according to prosecutors. Rather than investing the money, Sanchez converted a substantial portion into U.S. dollars through transactions designed to disguise where the funds came from and who controlled them. Prosecutors said he then used the money for his personal benefit. "Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm," Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas said. "In this case, the defendant exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate the trust of unsuspecting victims and deprive them of their money." U.S. District Judge Melissa Damian sentenced Sanchez to nearly four years behind bars and ordered him to pay restitution to his victims.

entry.title: St. Lucie County superintendent of schools promises review of district policies after historic flooding - WPBF
entry.summary: St. Lucie County superintendent of schools promises review of district policies after historic flooding    WPBF
entry.article_text: St. Lucie County Schools Superintendent Dr. Jon Prince apologized to the district Tuesday night and promised a review of all decisions and actions from the historic flooding on Nov. 2. "It was very stressful for our families, and I certainly apologize for the stress that they went through on that day," Prince said. A video from that day shows a boy getting off a school bus on SW Coleman Avenue in Port St. Lucie and walking through flood waters that reach as high as his chest. Critics have pointed to that video and questioned the actions of the school district. In an exclusive interview, Prince expressed regret over the events of Nov. 2, stating that decisions were made based on the information available at the time. He emphasized that the flooding was unexpected. "The bottom line is I don't know of anything that could have predicted what transpired as the day progressed," Prince said. Prince assured that every decision made that day is being analyzed. "We are going to review all our procedures, our policies to make sure that if there's anything that we could have done differently, that moving forward we will," he said. With heavy rain in the forecast, St. Lucie County Schools decided to cancel classes for Wednesday. Prince said he hopes the decision is an overreaction. At the same time, though, he does not want to take any chances. "The ground is so saturated, but if the conditions worsen tomorrow, we don't want a repeat of what happened November 2," Prince said. Prince said the district will monitor the weather Wednesday and decide late Wednesday afternoon if classes should be canceled again Thursday. He said they'll follow that model until they are sure it's safe for students to return to class. entry.title: 4 arrested after attempted home invasion at Palm City's Evergreen Club, sheriff says
entry.summary: Four people from Jacksonville, including a 16-year-old, are in custody after the Martin County Sheriff's Office says a 17-year-old heard a suspicious noise outside his family's home in Palm City's Evergreen Club, prompting a 911 call and an extensive overnight search. Investigators say the group parked a vehicle near the C-23 Canal before walking into the gated community and targeting a home. Deputies later recovered masks, gloves and a stolen firearm during their investigation. WATCH: Teen's Alert Leads to 4 Arrests After Palm City Manhunt Teen's Alert Leads to 4 Arrests After Palm City Manhunt | WPTV The sheriff's office is now asking residents in the Evergreen Club community to check their homes, vehicles and security cameras for anything suspicious as investigators try to determine why the group traveled from Jacksonville to Martin County and whether any other properties were targeted. Teen hears noise outside family's home Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the incident began just after 3 a.m., when the family's 17-year-old son realized something was wrong. 'The 17-year-old son heard a noise, woke up, knew something was wrong, but didn't quite know what it was,' Budensiek said. '(He) went and talked to his parents.' The family then began reviewing footage from security cameras around the property. According to Budensiek, one camera was no longer working properly. When the family went farther back through the recorded footage, he said they discovered people moving around the home. 'They could see that one of their cameras wasn't working,' Budensiek said. 'They kept going further back in their search history, and saw where these three black males actually were circling the house.' Budensiek said the video showed someone placing a sticker over a camera lens near the back door so activity there could no longer be seen. The family called 911. Deputies find suspected getaway vehicle Deputies began searching the area outside the gated community and checked a parking lot near the C-23 Canal. 'There indeed was a car parked there,' Budensiek said. The sheriff's office said the suspects had parked along the canal before walking into the neighborhood. One person was taken into custody near the vehicle, while the others fled, according to the sheriff. Deputies established a perimeter and searched with assistance from aviation and K-9 units and the Stuart Police Department. entry.title: IRC sheriff renews push for unified 911 dispatch as Vero Beach weighs Amendment 3 cuts - WPEC
entry.summary: IRC sheriff renews push for unified 911 dispatch as Vero Beach weighs Amendment 3 cuts    WPEC
entry.article_text: Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers asked the Vero Beach City Council on Tuesday to take another look at merging emergency dispatch. He pitched it as a way to save money as the city prepares for revenue losses under Amendment 3 . Flowers said he first brought the idea to the council about two years ago. He said Brevard County has since moved to a unified dispatch system, and he told council members his offer still stands. "I'm not asking for anything specific today. I just want to make sure that it's known that it is my desire that we go to a unified dispatch system," Flowers said. He asked that it be considered "as a potential cost savings" as the city makes what he called "difficult decisions" under Amendment 3. Florida voters approved a ballot initiative that will slash non-school property taxes despite a campaign by local officials warning it would gut funding for public safety and other services. It will increase the homestead exemption from about $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Council member Tracey Zudans asked city staff to put numbers on the idea. "I'd love to see some numbers attached to it, not just response time numbers, but also some dollar numbers so that we can share that with our taxpayers as well," Zudans said. "I'd be happy to have my staff work with you guys," Flowers said. Mayor Aaron Vos said city staff will total what the city spends on dispatch now, and Flowers will bring back what it would cost the city to join a countywide call center. Vos said he expects a unified center would be run by the county, not the sheriff, similar to St. Lucie County's. Vice Mayor John Cotugno asked whether the dispatch center would be a county function or run by the sheriff's office. Flowers said the county technically runs dispatch, but most dispatchers work for his agency. "I have the bulk of dispatchers that work for me at the sheriff's office, so I can only offer it from my side," Flowers said. "You would have to ask the county if they were interested in maybe doing it differently." He added that the sheriff's office and the county are still discussing how Amendment 3 will affect their relationship. See also: 22-year-old West Palm Beach motorcyclist struck, killed by SUV in Loxahatchee That relationship has been strained before. In July 2025 a budget debate erupted during an Indian River County Commission meeting, prompting the board to call a 15-minute recess after tensions flared between commissioners and Flowers. Flowers was requesting $93.5 million that year, while the county recommended a budget closer to $83.5 million. Commissioners ultimately voted to raise the sheriff's budget by $6.8 million, far less than he requested. Flowers later sued the commission , which then held a special meeting over the sheriff's budget. "This is a very deep issue," Flowers said. "If we do it as a county, if we do it under me, either way, I'm just trying to get all of our dispatchers in the same room together." Council members took no action on the proposal. Vos said Amendment 3 means the city has to consider every option. "With the implications of Amendment 3, we have to look at all aspects of where we can save money," Vos said. "If it saves us money, that's what we need to do." But Vos said moving dispatch out of the police department could come with a hidden cost. "You could lose some of that rapport between the call center staff and the officers due to familiarity," he said. Vos said he talked with police leaders in Sebastian and Fellsmere after Flowers first pitched the idea. He said Sebastian police used the sheriff's call center until 2007, then went back to running their own. Vero Beach Police Chief David Currey said his position on keeping the city's dispatch center has not changed. Vero Beach and Sebastian police are the only agencies in the county that run their own dispatch. "The dispatchers know the officers. They know the community members," Currey said. "If we don't have that under our umbrella, then I don't have control over any of that." Currey said the department switched to a new computer-aided dispatch and records management system in June. He said the department is working with the sheriff's office to connect the two agencies' dispatch systems, which would let dispatchers see where deputies and officers are and handle calls without transferring them. Currey said the idea last came up around 2012. He said the sheriff at the time told the city that dispatching for Vero Beach would likely cost about the same, if not more. "We have ten dispatchers, and they have salaries, and they have benefits," Currey said. "That will cost him just like it'll cost us." Despite the uncertainty around Amendment 3, Currey said the department is not freezing hiring and is interviewing for a police officer position now.

entry.title: West Palm Beach police officers deliver 150 Thanksgiving meals to residents in need
entry.summary: With Thanksgiving approaching, West Palm Beach police officers are helping make sure local families and individuals have a meal for the holiday. THE FUND , a nonprofit that supports the West Palm Beach Police Department, provided 150 Thanksgiving meals for officers to deliver to residents in need across the city. WATCH REPORT BELOW: West Palm Beach police deliver meals ahead of Thanksgiving Officers loaded the meals into police vehicles Tuesday morning at Heart and Soul Park on North Rosemary Avenue before taking them directly to residents' homes. According to organizers, police officers identified the families and individuals who could use additional support during the holiday season. The effort is a collaboration between THE FUND and the West Palm Beach Police Department. THE FUND is a nonprofit organization that works to supplement resources for the police department beyond what is available through the city's budget. The organization says its broader mission is to support officers while helping improve public safety and quality of life in West Palm Beach.

entry.title: Adopt-A-Family of the Palm Beaches helps local families find stability this holiday season
entry.summary: For some children, the biggest worry this holiday season should be who gets caught first in a game of hide-and-seek or who can throw a football the farthest. But for families facing housing insecurity, the reality can be much different. The nonprofit provides affordable and supportive housing for families experiencing homelessness or at risk of losing their homes. Its work also extends beyond housing, offering resources designed to help parents and children build long-term stability. At one of the organization's residential campuses, families live within walking distance of a playground, where children have a place to play while their parents work toward a more secure future. 'We are surrounded by 87 units of supportive housing which are located within a tenth of a mile of this playground,' said Matt Constantine, CEO of Adopt-A-Family of the Palm Beaches. Constantine says the campus setting allows the organization to bring several services directly to the families it serves. Those resources include educational support for children, after-school programming, career coaching, case management and on-site mental health services. The goal is to address the challenges that can make it difficult for families to remain housed and financially independent. 'Provide housing stability to families with children who are either experiencing homelessness or at risk of becoming homeless,' Constantine said, describing the organization's longstanding mission. But as housing costs continue to rise, the need for assistance is growing. 'Our phones ring all day long,' Constantine said. He says the upfront cost of securing a rental property can be a significant obstacle for families already struggling financially. Constantine says roughly two-thirds of the people served by Adopt-A-Family are children, making educational and emotional support an important part of its mission. entry.title: Neighbors plead for help as repeated flooding threatens their Indian River County homes
entry.summary: People across South Florida and the Treasure Coast are bracing for yet another round of heavy rain , and one Indian River County community is pleading for help after battling repeated flooding this month. Joe Waters documented his frustration Saturday evening, recording on his phone in front of his mobile home in the Heritage Plantation mobile home park near Vero Beach as a car drove through floodwaters that almost covered its headlights. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Mobile home park residents plead for help after repeated floods Waters said the wake caused by passing vehicles crashed into the bricks that protect the undercarriage of his home, toppling them. 'The water came up probably about thigh high,' Waters said. 'Came up into the driveway, went into the house.' Waters and his wife were able to clean their home, but he said his car is still in the shop with $4,600 worth of damage, waiting on approval from the insurance company. When we showed up at Heritage Plantation Tuesday afternoon, a crowd of neighbors gathered fed up after battling multiple floods just this month. Dawn Carboni, the HOA president, told me she wants to be a voice for her neighbors, especially those who can't speak up. 'They just want to feel safe in their homes,' she said. The flooding has created dangerous conditions for emergency responders, Carboni said. 'We had a gentleman who needed EMS to come out, and they could not get to his home, so they had to park out on 82nd (Avenue), and then a large fire truck had to get to the home,' Carboni said. With more heavy rain in the forecast, Carboni said residents are frightened. 'People are afraid. It's horrible living in fear when you don't know if it's going to rain and you're going to be able to leave your home the next day.' She wants to spread awareness about what her community is going through. 'We need help, and we're asking for help,' Carboni said. Emergency managers in Indian River County tell me they're operating at a Level 2 emergency, meaning the Emergency Operations Center is partially activated. They've extended the state of emergency through Sunday, Nov. 30. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: 4 taken into custody after overnight burglary, manhunt in Martin County
entry.summary: A homeowner's quick call to 911 helped interrupt an attempted home invasion in Palm City early Tuesday, leading to the arrests of four people from Jacksonville, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. The sheriff's office said the homeowner heard a noise outside a home on Southwest Bimini Circle in the Evergreen Club and contacted authorities. Investigators said at least one of the suspects was armed with a handgun. When deputies arrived, the four suspects scattered into the neighborhood, according to the sheriff's office. Deputies established a perimeter and, with assistance from the agency's aviation, drone and K-9 units and the Stuart Police Department K-9 unit, found all four hiding in separate locations throughout the community. Investigators believe the group parked near a canal and walked into the neighborhood to target the home. Deputies said they recovered a firearm, masks and gloves. Detectives later determined the gun had been reported stolen. The sheriff's office identified three of those arrested as 21-year-old Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr., 21-year-old Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews and 21-year-old Cameron Elijah Mapson. The fourth person arrested is 16 years old. WPTV is not naming the juvenile. All four face attempted home invasion charges and were taken into custody, according to the sheriff's office. Wise also faces charges of grand theft of a firearm and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. The sheriff's office credited the homeowner's quick decision to call authorities with interrupting the alleged crime before anyone was hurt.

entry.title: Man arrested after 19-year-old woman escapes attempted sexual assault in Boca Raton, police say
entry.summary: A 19-year-old woman escaped with minor injuries after police say a man armed with a knife forced her into a wooded area along Boca Ratons El Rio Trail and attempted to sexually assault her Monday morning. Boca Raton police said 36-year-old LaPaul Jackson was arrested a short time later aboard a public bus as he allegedly tried to leave the area. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Man arrested in Boca Raton after 19-year-old escapes attempted sexual assault Officers responded shortly after 11:30 a.m. to a report of an assault along the El Rio Trail, just north of Spanish River Boulevard. According to police, the woman was walking along the trail when a man she did not know approached her from behind with a knife. Investigators said he forced her into a nearby wooded area where a small camp had been set up. Police said the man attempted to sexually assault the woman and committed additional lewd acts before she was able to escape and run back toward the trail. Another person then called police. The woman suffered minor injuries and gave officers a detailed description of the suspect, police said. Officers established a perimeter and worked with the woman to track her cellphone, which police said the suspect had taken. Real-time location information showed the phone was moving, leading investigators to believe the suspect had boarded a public bus. Officers stopped the bus near North Federal Highway and Northeast 20th Street. Police said they identified Jackson aboard the bus and recovered the woman's cellphone. Jackson was arrested on charges of armed kidnapping, armed robbery and attempted sexual battery. Police said additional charges are pending. He was later taken to the Palm Beach County Jail. The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with information is asked to contact Boca Raton police Detective Gannon at 561-620-6073.

entry.title: Neighbors plead for help as repeated flooding threatens their Indian River County homes - WFLX
entry.summary: Neighbors plead for help as repeated flooding threatens their Indian River County homes    WFLX
entry.article_text: People across South Florida and the Treasure Coast are bracing for yet another round of heavy rain , and one Indian River County community is pleading for help after battling repeated flooding this month. Joe Waters documented his frustration Saturday evening, recording on his phone in front of his mobile home in the Heritage Plantation mobile home park near Vero Beach as a car drove through floodwaters that almost covered its headlights. Waters said the wake caused by passing vehicles crashed into the bricks that protect the undercarriage of his home, toppling them. “The water came up probably about thigh high,” Waters said. “Came up into the driveway, went into the house.” Waters and his wife were able to clean their home, but he said his car is still in the shop with $4,600 worth of damage, waiting on approval from the insurance company. When we showed up at Heritage Plantation Tuesday afternoon, a crowd of neighbors gathered — fed up after battling multiple floods just this month. Dawn Carboni, the HOA president, told me she wants to be a voice for her neighbors, especially those who can’t speak up. “They just want to feel safe in their homes,” she said. The flooding has created dangerous conditions for emergency responders, Carboni said. “We had a gentleman who needed EMS to come out, and they could not get to his home, so they had to park out on 82nd (Avenue), and then a large fire truck had to get to the home,” Carboni said. With more heavy rain in the forecast, Carboni said residents are frightened. It’s horrible living in fear when you don’t know if it’s going to rain and you’re going to be able to leave your home the next day.” She wants to spread awareness about what her community is going through. “We need help, and we’re asking for help,” Carboni said. Emergency managers in Indian River County tell me they’re operating at a Level 2 emergency, meaning the Emergency Operations Center is partially activated. They’ve extended the state of emergency through Sunday, Nov. 30. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: 'Busiest shopping day': Fort Pierce businesses urge community to shop local on Small Business Saturday - WPBF
entry.summary: 'Busiest shopping day': Fort Pierce businesses urge community to shop local on Small Business Saturday    WPBF
entry.article_text: Small Business Saturday is just around the corner, and downtown Fort Pierce business owners are urging shoppers to support local stores as the holiday shopping season begins. Small Business Saturday was created by American Express in 2010 to get more customers through the doors of small businesses the Saturday after Thanksgiving. Small business owners in Fort Pierce are hoping you will shop small Saturday, and they're hoping you'll do it right here. The Executive Director of Main Street Fort Pierce, Michelle Chaffee Cavalcanti and volunteers have been reminding business owners about the significance of Small Business Saturday. "Thank you so much for participating with Shop Small with us. Thank you, we appreciate it," Chaffee Cavalcanti said. Juline Gurney, the owner of I Am Activeware, reflected on last year’s event, saying, "Last year I feel like there was a lot of new businesses, including myself, and downtown is a great spot to be. I had many visitors, to be exact 19 visitors that day, and my sales paid my rent that month." Newcomer, Kim Brant, the owner of Sunshine State of Mind Boutique, is excited about this weekend's event. "Last year I feel like there was a lot of new businesses, including myself, and downtown is a great spot to be," Brant said. This is year number nine for Beryl Muise, the owner of Notions Potions candles and more. Muise says Small Business Saturday is the most important shopping day of the year. "So that is our busiest shopping day of the entire year for us. And with that, retail has a very short window to make their money for the year, and so Shop Small Saturday kicks that off," Muise said. Main Street Fort Pierce is hosting the event, and organizers emphasized the importance of supporting local businesses, especially as some struggle to stock their shelves. "For a small business, putting the merchandise on the shelf is the equivalent of putting food on the table. They can't be separated," Chaffee Cavalcanti said. Shopping locally also benefits the community, organizers said. "And remember when you spend a dollar in a small business, $0.68 of that dollar stays in your community. That gives the ability for your money to do more, spread wider, and have a longer impact," Chaffee Cavalcanti said. Shoppers will also have the chance to participate in a raffle to win hundreds of dollars in gift cards. The shops in downtown Fort Pierce will open at 10 a.m. Saturday, and raffle tickets must be submitted by 5:30 p.m. The drawing will take place at 6 p.m. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.
