entry.title: IRC sheriff renews push for unified 911 dispatch as Vero Beach weighs Amendment 3 cuts - WPEC
entry.summary: IRC sheriff renews push for unified 911 dispatch as Vero Beach weighs Amendment 3 cuts    WPEC
entry.article_text: Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers asked the Vero Beach City Council on Tuesday to take another look at merging emergency dispatch. He pitched it as a way to save money as the city prepares for revenue losses under Amendment 3 . Flowers said he first brought the idea to the council about two years ago. He said Brevard County has since moved to a unified dispatch system, and he told council members his offer still stands. "I'm not asking for anything specific today. I just want to make sure that it's known that it is my desire that we go to a unified dispatch system," Flowers said. He asked that it be considered "as a potential cost savings" as the city makes what he called "difficult decisions" under Amendment 3. Florida voters approved a ballot initiative that will slash non-school property taxes despite a campaign by local officials warning it would gut funding for public safety and other services. It will increase the homestead exemption from about $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Council member Tracey Zudans asked city staff to put numbers on the idea. "I'd love to see some numbers attached to it, not just response time numbers, but also some dollar numbers so that we can share that with our taxpayers as well," Zudans said. "I'd be happy to have my staff work with you guys," Flowers said. Mayor Aaron Vos said city staff will total what the city spends on dispatch now, and Flowers will bring back what it would cost the city to join a countywide call center. Vos said he expects a unified center would be run by the county, not the sheriff, similar to St. Lucie County's. Vice Mayor John Cotugno asked whether the dispatch center would be a county function or run by the sheriff's office. Flowers said the county technically runs dispatch, but most dispatchers work for his agency. "I have the bulk of dispatchers that work for me at the sheriff's office, so I can only offer it from my side," Flowers said. "You would have to ask the county if they were interested in maybe doing it differently." He added that the sheriff's office and the county are still discussing how Amendment 3 will affect their relationship. See also: 22-year-old West Palm Beach motorcyclist struck, killed by SUV in Loxahatchee That relationship has been strained before. In July 2025 a budget debate erupted during an Indian River County Commission meeting, prompting the board to call a 15-minute recess after tensions flared between commissioners and Flowers. Flowers was requesting $93.5 million that year, while the county recommended a budget closer to $83.5 million. Commissioners ultimately voted to raise the sheriff's budget by $6.8 million, far less than he requested. Flowers later sued the commission , which then held a special meeting over the sheriff's budget. "This is a very deep issue," Flowers said. "If we do it as a county, if we do it under me, either way, I'm just trying to get all of our dispatchers in the same room together." Council members took no action on the proposal. Vos said Amendment 3 means the city has to consider every option. "With the implications of Amendment 3, we have to look at all aspects of where we can save money," Vos said. "If it saves us money, that's what we need to do." But Vos said moving dispatch out of the police department could come with a hidden cost. "You could lose some of that rapport between the call center staff and the officers due to familiarity," he said. Vos said he talked with police leaders in Sebastian and Fellsmere after Flowers first pitched the idea. He said Sebastian police used the sheriff's call center until 2007, then went back to running their own. Vero Beach Police Chief David Currey said his position on keeping the city's dispatch center has not changed. Vero Beach and Sebastian police are the only agencies in the county that run their own dispatch. "The dispatchers know the officers. They know the community members," Currey said. "If we don't have that under our umbrella, then I don't have control over any of that." Currey said the department switched to a new computer-aided dispatch and records management system in June. He said the department is working with the sheriff's office to connect the two agencies' dispatch systems, which would let dispatchers see where deputies and officers are and handle calls without transferring them. Currey said the idea last came up around 2012. He said the sheriff at the time told the city that dispatching for Vero Beach would likely cost about the same, if not more. "We have ten dispatchers, and they have salaries, and they have benefits," Currey said. "That will cost him just like it'll cost us." Despite the uncertainty around Amendment 3, Currey said the department is not freezing hiring and is interviewing for a police officer position now.

entry.title: 'A huge loss’: Family remembers 24-year-old killed in Port St. Lucie hit-and-run - WPEC
entry.summary: 'A huge loss’: Family remembers 24-year-old killed in Port St. Lucie hit-and-run    WPEC
entry.article_text: A Port St. Lucie family is remembering their 24-year-old daughter after she was killed in a hit-and-run last week. Alexis Cuellar, known to her family as Lexi, was riding her scooter to work on Nov. 16 when she was struck by a vehicle near SW Gatlin Boulevard, according to police. She died the following day, Nov. 17. For the first time, her father and relatives are sharing memories of the young woman they say brought joy to everyone around her. Alexis wasn't just a ray of sunshine, you know. I think to us she was just the sun, her father, Alberto Vasquez, said As the eldest daughter, Vasquez said Alexis had a natural instinct to care for others, beginning with her own siblings. Ever since she was born she just, she had a passion for caring for others, starting with her siblings, you know, he said. At the family's Port St. Lucie home, Vasquez and relatives, some visiting from Texas, gathered around photos of Alexis as they remembered her life. She was the sweetest person ever, and it's a huge loss for the family, her aunt, Minerva Benitez, said. Also read: Port St. Lucie hit-and-run victim dies; driver could face more serious charges Vasquez said the support they have received has helped them. It's really helped us get through these first difficult days that were unbearable, he said. He remembered his daughter as someone who loved children and dreamed of working with them. He was also proud of her time in Junior ROTC. On the morning of the crash, Vasquez watched Alexis leave home for her job at Wendy's. She had been excited about picking up more hours. He said he saw her riding away on her scooter and assumed she would be OK. Five minutes later, he learned there had been a crash. Police have charged 18-year-old Tristian Ray Sanchez-Chasmer in connection with the crash. Investigators say he had been playing ding-dong-ditch with friends before getting behind the wheel of a Chevy Tahoe. He's accused of hitting Cuellar as she rode her scooter in a crosswalk, then leaving the scene. He is currently charged with leaving the scene. Additional charges, including vehicular homicide, could follow. Vasquez said he wishes he could have been there to help his daughter. I'm sorry that I couldn't be there for her, maybe help her. And that I loved her deeply because I didn't get a chance to tell her that, he said. Now, he is preparing a place at home where he plans to bring her. A service for Alexis will be held Wednesday, Nov. 25, at Haisley Funeral Home in Fort Pierce. Police are continuing to investigate the crash.

entry.title: 4 arrested after attempted home invasion at Palm City's Evergreen Club, sheriff says - WFLX
entry.summary: 4 arrested after attempted home invasion at Palm City's Evergreen Club, sheriff says    WFLX
entry.article_text: Four people from Jacksonville, including a 16-year-old, are in custody after the Martin County Sheriff's Office says a 17-year-old heard a suspicious noise outside his family's home in Palm City's Evergreen Club, prompting a 911 call and an extensive overnight search. Investigators say the group parked a vehicle near the C-23 Canal before walking into the gated community and targeting a home. Deputies later recovered masks, gloves and a stolen firearm during their investigation. WATCH: Teen's Alert Leads to 4 Arrests After Palm City Manhunt The sheriff's office is now asking residents in the Evergreen Club community to check their homes, vehicles and security cameras for anything suspicious as investigators try to determine why the group traveled from Jacksonville to Martin County and whether any other properties were targeted. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the incident began just after 3 a.m., when the family's 17-year-old son realized something was wrong. "The 17-year-old son heard a noise, woke up, knew something was wrong, but didn't quite know what it was," Budensiek said. "(He) went and talked to his parents." The family then began reviewing footage from security cameras around the property. According to Budensiek, one camera was no longer working properly. When the family went farther back through the recorded footage, he said they discovered people moving around the home. "They could see that one of their cameras wasn't working," Budensiek said. "They kept going further back in their search history, and saw where these three black males actually were circling the house." Budensiek said the video showed someone placing a sticker over a camera lens near the back door so activity there could no longer be seen. Deputies began searching the area outside the gated community and checked a parking lot near the C-23 Canal. "There indeed was a car parked there," Budensiek said. The sheriff's office said the suspects had parked along the canal before walking into the neighborhood. One person was taken into custody near the vehicle, while the others fled, according to the sheriff. Deputies established a perimeter and searched with assistance from aviation and K-9 units and the Stuart Police Department. Budensiek said two of the people who fled were ultimately discovered hiding beneath the bridge carrying Murphy Road over the C-23 Canal. "Two fled and ended up hiding under the bridge that crosses the C-23 Canal on Murphy Road," Budensiek said. "They were the last two to actually be apprehended after an extensive manhunt." The three adults arrested were identified as 21-year-old Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr., 21-year-old Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews and 21-year-old Cameron Elijah Mapson. A 16-year-old was also arrested, but WPTV is not identifying the juvenile. All four face attempted home invasion charges, according to published reports citing the sheriff's office. Wise also faces grand theft of a firearm and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. As investigators retraced the route between the suspects' vehicle and the family's home, Budensiek said they recovered a handgun. "They recovered a handgun that was stolen with an extended magazine, and were able to corroborate again what the intended victim said," Budensiek said. The Sheriff's Office has also reported recovering masks and gloves during the investigation. Investigators are now trying to determine why this particular home may have been targeted. "We don't know why that house," Budensiek said. "We don't know if they went to any other houses potentially in the middle of the night." The sheriff's office is asking residents to review their security footage and inspect their homes and vehicles for missing property or possible evidence of another attempted break-in. Anyone who discovers missing property or signs of a break-in is asked to contact the Martin County Sheriff's Office at 772-220-7060. Investigators are also examining digital evidence as they work to establish why the four made the trip from Jacksonville to Palm City. entry.summary: In Fort Pierce, behind the doors of A Future Worth Fighting 4, they embody what the City stands for. Here, this community is a big fighting community. If youre from Fort Pierce, you know how we get down, said Owner, Darrion Henry. How they get down at A Future Worth Fighting 4 was on full display at the 2026 Florida State Police Athletic League. WATCH: A local boxing gym brings the two C's: community and championships A local boxing gym brings the two C's: community and championships They finished with three state champions, a silver medalist, and a second-place overall team finish, and the star of the Tournament was none other than Justice Henry. He credits the gym's family-like atmosphere and tough-love environment for his success. This gym has been the biggest part of my life. Ive been boxing since I was eight years old, and this became a home for our own little community and us, with everyone we bring in here, said Henry. While Henry has been boxing since he was eight, he has a teammate, Frantzner Jean, whos just getting started but is already making a name for himself after winning his first fight by unanimous decision. It felt pretty fun; I just like the dopamine rush from it, said Jean. Every day after school, kids fill the gym to learn the sweet science of boxing, but there's one rule: you have to go to school every day. Im a teacher at Dan McCarty, so I can see how their behavior has changed, and now I have a lot of kids who show up to school because they know if they dont show up to school, Im going to get on them, said Henry. One of the kids taking the school-first approach is Michael Sanchez, whose dad signed him up for classes, but now hes ready to take this sport as far as it can go. I ended up liking it because I can learn from it, like discipline and hard work, said Sanchez.

According to FHP, all northbound lanes reopened at 1:56 p.m. As of 3 p.m. the right shoulder is still blocked, according to Florida 511. The crash involved a medium-duty truck hauling a trailer loaded with pallets of mulch and a sport utility vehicle. Both vehicles were traveling northbound when the truck jackknifed and struck the wall and the SUV. Four individuals were transported to Florida Coast Medical Center, and one was transported to Martin Memorial South. Photos from the scene show multiple emergency vehicles and large trucks at the scene. Cars were also seen on the grass shoulder. The incident is classified as major. According to the Florida Highway Patrol , injuries are associated with the incident. K9's were able to track down all four suspects hiding in separate locations throughout the community. The sheriff's office says at least one of the suspects was armed. Further investigation revealed that the suspects parked along the canal and walked into the neighborhood to target the home. The sheriff's office says during the apprehension they uncovered masks, a firearm and gloves. The suspects were identified as: Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr, 21 Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews, 21 Cameron Elijah Mapson, 21 Teenage boy, 16 All four were charged with an attempted home invasion and were taken to the Martin County Jail. Wise faces an additional charge of grand theft and possession of a firearm. See also: Boca Raton police arrest man after reported assault on El Rio Trail The agency is asking Palm City residents to check their homes and vehicles for missing property or signs of a break-in. entry.title: Bodycam shows El Rio Trail assault arrest, people call for more police presence
entry.summary: New police body-camera video shows officers taking a man into custody after a 19-year-old woman reported being attacked along Boca Ratons El Rio Trail. Now, people who frequent the trail say the attack, along with an earlier incident involving the same suspect at the same location, is making them reconsider their safety and call for a greater police presence. WATCH: El Rio Trail assault arrest caught on bodycam amid safety concerns Bodycam shows El Rio Trail assault arrest, people call for more police presence Bodycam shows suspect being taken into custody Police body-camera video shows officers taking 36-year-old LaPaul Jackson of Miami Gardens into custody following Mondays attack. According to a Boca Raton police report, the 19-year-old woman was walking along El Rio Trail around 11:30 a.m. when Jackson allegedly approached her from behind with a knife and forced her into a wooded area. Police said the woman was attacked before she managed to escape and return to the trail, where someone helped her call 911. Investigators said she suffered multiple cuts. Police used the location of the womans stolen cellphone to track Jackson to a Palm Tran bus, according to the police affidavit. Jackson faces seven charges, including kidnapping, sexual battery with a deadly weapon, robbery with a weapon and tampering with a victim. Police records also show he is accused of violating his pretrial release in connection with an August robbery case. Attack raises safety concerns along El Rio Trail People who regularly walk and exercise along El Rio Trail told WPTV the daytime attack has changed how they think about their safety. In shock, especially because it happened so early in the morning, Isabel Chambers told WPTV. Luiz Souza said he was disappointed and believes more attention needs to be paid to the area. Disappointment because the police is supposed to take care a little better of this place, Souza said. Another person said the attack will make her reconsider walking the trail by herself. Well, Im going to think twice now about going alone, she said. Previous incident adds to concerns The concerns come as WPTV learned Jackson had previously been arrested in connection with another incident at the same location on El Rio Trail. According to police records, Jackson allegedly pushed a woman to the ground and stole her cellphone during an Aug. 1 incident. The affidavit says Jackson was on pretrial release in that case when the November incident occurred. Marvin Montoya

entry.title: Project Tango attorney threatened legal action days before Palm Beach County approved data center expansion
entry.summary: An attorney for the developer behind the controversial Project Tango data center warned Palm Beach County of 'significant and potentially catastrophic financial liability' if an expansion wasn't approved, according to a 180-page letter obtained by WPTV's Michael Hoffman. Ten days after the letter was sent, Palm Beach County zoning staff approved the expansion. The letter represents a new development in WPTV's nearly yearlong coverage of Project Tango and raises new questions about the October decision that allowed the project to triple its data center space without another vote by county commissioners. In July, Palm Beach County commissioners denied a separate proposal to expand the project. Then in October, county staff administratively approved another expansion. The letter from Project Tango attorney Ethan Loeb was sent before that October approval and threatened significant legal action if county staff did not approve the expansion. Letter warns of 'catastrophic financial liability' The 180-page letter included legal threats against Palm Beach County and a personal threat of legal action against county Zoning Director Wendy Hernandez. According to the letter, denying the expansion could result in 'significant and potentially catastrophic financial liability.' The letter went further, contending potential damages involving PBA Holdings could be 'so significant that it would be impossible for the county to financially sustain the damages that PBA Holdings would recover.' Ten days later, zoning staff approved the expansion. Hoffman spoke with District 6 Commissioner Katherine Waldron, who represents the area where the project would be located. Waldron said she believes the letter's threat against a county employee calls the approval process into question. 'That letter comes out threatening not just the county, but to one of our zoning people, and I think that that corrupts the process, and we should consider overturning the decision because of that,' Waldron said. entry.article_text: Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers asked the Vero Beach City Council on Tuesday to take another look at merging emergency dispatch. He pitched it as a way to save money as the city prepares for revenue losses under Amendment 3 . Flowers said he first brought the idea to the council about two years ago. He said Brevard County has since moved to a unified dispatch system, and he told council members his offer still stands. "I'm not asking for anything specific today. I just want to make sure that it's known that it is my desire that we go to a unified dispatch system," Flowers said. He asked that it be considered "as a potential cost savings" as the city makes what he called "difficult decisions" under Amendment 3. Florida voters approved a ballot initiative that will slash non-school property taxes despite a campaign by local officials warning it would gut funding for public safety and other services. It will increase the homestead exemption from about $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Council member Tracey Zudans asked city staff to put numbers on the idea. "I'd love to see some numbers attached to it, not just response time numbers, but also some dollar numbers so that we can share that with our taxpayers as well," Zudans said. "I'd be happy to have my staff work with you guys," Flowers said. Mayor Aaron Vos said city staff will total what the city spends on dispatch now, and Flowers will bring back what it would cost the city to join a countywide call center. Vos said he expects a unified center would be run by the county, not the sheriff, similar to St. Lucie County's. Vice Mayor John Cotugno asked whether the dispatch center would be a county function or run by the sheriff's office. Flowers said the county technically runs dispatch, but most dispatchers work for his agency. "I have the bulk of dispatchers that work for me at the sheriff's office, so I can only offer it from my side," Flowers said. "You would have to ask the county if they were interested in maybe doing it differently." He added that the sheriff's office and the county are still discussing how Amendment 3 will affect their relationship. See also: 22-year-old West Palm Beach motorcyclist struck, killed by SUV in Loxahatchee That relationship has been strained before. In July 2025 a budget debate erupted during an Indian River County Commission meeting, prompting the board to call a 15-minute recess after tensions flared between commissioners and Flowers. Flowers was requesting $93.5 million that year, while the county recommended a budget closer to $83.5 million. Commissioners ultimately voted to raise the sheriff's budget by $6.8 million, far less than he requested. Flowers later sued the commission , which then held a special meeting over the sheriff's budget. "This is a very deep issue," Flowers said. "If we do it as a county, if we do it under me, either way, I'm just trying to get all of our dispatchers in the same room together." Council members took no action on the proposal. Vos said Amendment 3 means the city has to consider every option. "With the implications of Amendment 3, we have to look at all aspects of where we can save money," Vos said. "If it saves us money, that's what we need to do." But Vos said moving dispatch out of the police department could come with a hidden cost. "You could lose some of that rapport between the call center staff and the officers due to familiarity," he said. Vos said he talked with police leaders in Sebastian and Fellsmere after Flowers first pitched the idea. He said Sebastian police used the sheriff's call center until 2007, then went back to running their own. Vero Beach Police Chief David Currey said his position on keeping the city's dispatch center has not changed. Vero Beach and Sebastian police are the only agencies in the county that run their own dispatch. "The dispatchers know the officers. They know the community members," Currey said. "If we don't have that under our umbrella, then I don't have control over any of that." Currey said the department switched to a new computer-aided dispatch and records management system in June. He said the department is working with the sheriff's office to connect the two agencies' dispatch systems, which would let dispatchers see where deputies and officers are and handle calls without transferring them. Currey said the idea last came up around 2012. He said the sheriff at the time told the city that dispatching for Vero Beach would likely cost about the same, if not more. "We have ten dispatchers, and they have salaries, and they have benefits," Currey said. "That will cost him just like it'll cost us." Despite the uncertainty around Amendment 3, Currey said the department is not freezing hiring and is interviewing for a police officer position now.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie man gets 47 months in federal prison for $260K N3ON deepfake cryptoscam - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie man gets 47 months in federal prison for $260K N3ON deepfake cryptoscam    WPEC
entry.article_text: A fake online persona, an AI-generated voice and a $260,000 cryptocurrency payday. Federal prosecutors say a Port St. Lucie man used all three to pull off an elaborate fraud scheme involving a popular internet streamer. 36,-year-old David Anthony Sanchez, also known as "Dave the Jewler," was sentenced to 47 months in federal prison Tuesday after pleading guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida . The scheme centered on popular online streamer N3ON , whose identity Sanchez hijacked to convince organizers of a cryptocurrency project that the internet personality was backing their investment. According to federal court records, Sanchez created fake online accounts posing as N3ON and his representative, communicating directly with organizers of a cryptocurrency "memecoin" project . But the impersonation went beyond fake profiles. Prosecutors said Sanchez used artificial intelligence to generate an audio recording mimicking N3ON's voice, falsely confirming the streamer's involvement in the project. Sanchez also signed agreements using N3ON's identity, further convincing organizers that the endorsement was legitimate. See also: Riviera Beach mayor calls for volunteers, supplies to aid Lone Pine Estates flood recovery The deception worked. Believing they had secured the streamer's participation, the victims transferred approximately $260,000 in cryptocurrency to accounts controlled by Sanchez, according to prosecutors. Rather than investing the money, Sanchez converted a substantial portion into U.S. dollars through transactions designed to disguise where the funds came from and who controlled them. Prosecutors said he then used the money for his personal benefit. "Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm," Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas said. "In this case, the defendant exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate the trust of unsuspecting victims and deprive them of their money." U.S. District Judge Melissa Damian sentenced Sanchez to nearly four years behind bars and ordered him to pay restitution to his victims.

entry.title: 4 men arrested after attempted home invasion at Martin County’s Evergreen Club - WPEC
entry.summary: 4 men arrested after attempted home invasion at Martin County’s Evergreen Club    WPEC
entry.article_text: A Palm City teenager's quick thinking may have stopped four men from breaking into his family's home at the Evergreen Club community off Murphy Road. The Martin County Sheriff's Office says the 17-year-old boy heard a noise outside their home on SW Bimini Circle at 3 a.m. Tuesday. He alerted his parents who called 911, interrupting the home invasion. When deputies arrived at the scene, the four suspects, three men and a teenager from Jacksonville, ran away in different directions. The sheriff's office says deputies set up a perimeter around the neighborhood with help from its aviation team, K-9 unit, and the Stuart Police Department. K9's were able to track down all four suspects hiding in separate locations throughout the community. The teen was found hiding in a bush outside the community. Two of the men were found hiding under a nearby bridge off Murphy Road. The fourth person was in a nearby parking lot who detectives believe was the getaway driver. The sheriff's office says at least one of the suspects was armed with a handgun. Sheriff John Budensiek said three of the four suspects have violent criminal histories. "These are bad, bad individuals who drove at least three and a half hours to Martin County to victimize a family that was going throughout their normal nightly routines," Budensiek said. Investigators said the suspects parked along the canal and walked half a mile into the neighborhood to target the home. The group is seen on home security video around 3 a.m. wearing dark clothing, masks and gloves. The sheriff said they tried to break in through a back door and covered a surveillance camera lens with a sticker. Deputies found masks, gloves and a firearm that had been stolen. Homeowners at the Evergreen Club community were shaken up. "I immediately woke up to Facebook and texts this morning, friends and family asked me if I was okay," said resident Katherine Willis. "Absolutely shocked that they would try to come in here. What are you going to get out of here? It's just very out of the ordinary for sure." The suspects were identified as: Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr, 22 Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews, 21 Cameron Elijah Mapson, 21 Teenage boy, 16 All four were charged with attempted home invasion. Wise faces an additional charge of grand theft and possession of a firearm. They're all being held in the Martin County Jail without bond. See also: Boca Raton police arrest man after reported assault on El Rio Trail The agency is asking Palm City residents to check their homes and vehicles for missing property or signs of a break-in. Anyone who finds anything missing should call the sheriff’s office at 772-220-7060. "The Martin County Sheriff's Office is heavily invested in protecting our community," Budensiek said. "To these traveling criminals, we're gonna put you away forever if we can."

entry.title: Palm City family confronts masked intruders during attempted home invasion - WPBF
entry.summary: Palm City family confronts masked intruders during attempted home invasion    WPBF
entry.article_text: A Palm City family was shaken early Tuesday morning when three masked men, at least one armed, attempted to break into their home on Bimini Circle. The homeowner asked WPBF 25 News to not use their names but said his 17-year-old son was the first to hear the suspects as they tried to get in around 3 a.m. In an exclusive statement, the homeowner said, "My son heard them trying to jiggle open all three of our patio sliders fairly aggressively." The son woke his mother and father, and the father armed himself. "I grabbed my AR-15 and proceeded into the house as she called 911," he said. The homeowner believes the suspects got spooked after he turned off the outside lights. "They must have seen me through the windows and seen the lights go out and left," he said. "We're a bit shook from the experience but doing good and feel blessed and lucky." Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said his office deployed every resource they had to find the suspects. "We knew these were bad guys," he said. Authorities launched an extensive search for the suspects, using aerial resources and K-9 units. One suspect was found hiding in bushes outside the community, another near what they believe was the getaway car, and two others were discovered under a nearby bridge. The Sheriff's Office identified the suspects as 21-year-old Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr., 21-year-old Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews, and 21-year-old Cameron Elijah Mapson. A fourth suspect is 16 years old. All four suspects are charged with attempted home invasion and are being held at the Martin County jail without bond. The sheriff said the suspects are from Jacksonville, and three of them have extensive criminal records. "These are bad, bad individuals who drove at least three and a half hours to Martin County to victimize a family that was going about their normal nightly routines," Budensiek said. One question investigators are still trying to answer is why the suspects chose this particular home. Budensiek said it's unclear if the attack was random or if the family was targeted. "We don't know the answer to that. We don't know why that house. We don't know if they went to any other houses potentially in the middle of the night," Budensiek said. Authorities are asking residents in the area to check their cameras, cars, and homes for any signs of suspicious activity and to contact the sheriff's office with any information. entry.summary: 4 arrested after attempted home invasion at Palm City's Evergreen Club, sheriff says    WFLX
entry.article_text: Four people from Jacksonville, including a 16-year-old, are in custody after the Martin County Sheriff's Office says a 17-year-old heard a suspicious noise outside his family's home in Palm City's Evergreen Club, prompting a 911 call and an extensive overnight search. Investigators say the group parked a vehicle near the C-23 Canal before walking into the gated community and targeting a home. Deputies later recovered masks, gloves and a stolen firearm during their investigation. WATCH: Teen's Alert Leads to 4 Arrests After Palm City Manhunt The sheriff's office is now asking residents in the Evergreen Club community to check their homes, vehicles and security cameras for anything suspicious as investigators try to determine why the group traveled from Jacksonville to Martin County and whether any other properties were targeted. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the incident began just after 3 a.m., when the family's 17-year-old son realized something was wrong. "The 17-year-old son heard a noise, woke up, knew something was wrong, but didn't quite know what it was," Budensiek said. "(He) went and talked to his parents." The family then began reviewing footage from security cameras around the property. According to Budensiek, one camera was no longer working properly. When the family went farther back through the recorded footage, he said they discovered people moving around the home. "They could see that one of their cameras wasn't working," Budensiek said. "They kept going further back in their search history, and saw where these three black males actually were circling the house." Budensiek said the video showed someone placing a sticker over a camera lens near the back door so activity there could no longer be seen. Deputies began searching the area outside the gated community and checked a parking lot near the C-23 Canal. "There indeed was a car parked there," Budensiek said. The sheriff's office said the suspects had parked along the canal before walking into the neighborhood. One person was taken into custody near the vehicle, while the others fled, according to the sheriff. Deputies established a perimeter and searched with assistance from aviation and K-9 units and the Stuart Police Department. Budensiek said two of the people who fled were ultimately discovered hiding beneath the bridge carrying Murphy Road over the C-23 Canal. "Two fled and ended up hiding under the bridge that crosses the C-23 Canal on Murphy Road," Budensiek said. "They were the last two to actually be apprehended after an extensive manhunt." The three adults arrested were identified as 21-year-old Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr., 21-year-old Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews and 21-year-old Cameron Elijah Mapson. A 16-year-old was also arrested, but WPTV is not identifying the juvenile. All four face attempted home invasion charges, according to published reports citing the sheriff's office. entry.title: Sheriff renews call for unified 911 dispatch as Vero Beach faces Amendment 3 cuts - Sebastian Daily
entry.summary: Sheriff renews call for unified 911 dispatch as Vero Beach faces Amendment 3 cuts    Sebastian Daily
entry.article_text: Home Business News and Economic Updates in Sebastian, Florida Sheriff renews call for unified 911 dispatch as Vero Beach faces Amendment 3 cuts by Tina Hodges Nov 25, 2026 / 9:35 AM A A A A Reset Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers (City of Vero Beach) Share on Twitter Share via Email VERO BEACH— Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers stood before the Vero Beach City Council on Tuesday and asked council members to reconsider combining the city’s emergency dispatch with the sheriff’s office. He said unifying dispatch across the county has been one of his goals since taking office. “One of my goals since being elected sheriff was to unify public safety dispatch for our entire county under one roof,” Flowers told Sebastian Daily . “St. Lucie and others have had this for decades, and it just makes sense from a safety standpoint, communications perspective, and an overall reduction of duplicative services. It’s my hope that with Amendment 3 passing, as cities look to find ways to reduce costs, a unified public safety dispatch system will be one of the first choices.” He originally raised the idea with the council about two years ago. Since then, Brevard County has moved to a single dispatch center. Flowers hopes the city will consider the concept as it works through what he called “difficult decisions” under the amendment. Voters approved Amendment 3 earlier this month to raise the homestead exemption on non-school property taxes from roughly $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and to $250,000 in 2028. Local officials had opposed the measure, warning it would cut into funding for public safety and other services. Council member Tracey Zudans asked for concrete numbers. “I’d love to see some numbers attached to it, not just response time numbers, but also some dollar numbers so that we can share that with our taxpayers as well,” she said. Flowers said his staff would work with the city on the figures. Mayor Aaron Vos said staff will first calculate what the city currently spends on dispatch, and Flowers will come back with an estimate of what it would cost the city to join a countywide center. Vos said he expects the county, not the sheriff’s office, would run any unified operation — the same arrangement used in St. Lucie County. Vice Mayor John Cotugno asked whether the center would be a county function or under the sheriff. Flowers said the county technically oversees dispatch, though most of the dispatchers work for his agency. “I have the bulk of dispatchers that work for me at the sheriff’s office, so I can only offer it from my side,” he said. “You would have to ask the county if they were interested in maybe doing it differently.” Council members took no formal action on the proposal. entry.title: Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast residents eligible for federal aid after storms, flooding
entry.summary: Federal disaster aid is now available for residents in Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast affected by recent flooding. FEMA announced late Tuesday that federal disaster assistance is available to individuals and families in Indian River, Martin, Okeechobee, Palm Beach, St. Lucie and Brevard counties as recovery efforts continue. U.S. Rep. Lois Frankel said in a statement the declaration unlocks critical federal recovery resources for residents, businesses and local governments devastated by the flooding. The assistance can include grants for temporary housing and home repairs, low-cost loans to cover uninsured property losses and other programs designed to help people recover from the disaster. Residents who suffered damage or other losses should first file a claim with their insurance provider. They can then apply for FEMA assistance through DisasterAssistance.gov , by calling 1-800-621-3362 or through the FEMA App . Those who use a relay service, including video relay or captioned telephone services, should provide FEMA with the number for that service when applying. Federal funding is also available on a cost-sharing basis to state, tribal and eligible local governments, as well as certain private nonprofit organizations, for debris removal and emergency protective measures. That assistance is available in Palm Beach, Martin, Indian River, Okeechobee, Brevard and Hardee, counties. Frankel said that Palm Beach County officials estimate that $53 million in disaster assistance is needed countywide nearly $35 million to help individuals and families recover and more than $18 million to help local governments cover emergency response and cleanup costs. Additional counties could be designated for federal assistance later, depending on the results of continuing damage assessments. What residents should do: File a claim with their insurance provider. Apply for federal assistance at DisasterAssistance.gov , through the FEMA App or by calling 1-800-621-3362. Severe storms and flooding have impacted parts of Florida since Oct. 31, prompting the state to ask for the federal disaster declaration.

entry.title: Fort Pierce boxing gym builds champions in the ring and community through discipline
entry.summary: In Fort Pierce, behind the doors of A Future Worth Fighting 4, they embody what the City stands for. Here, this community is a big fighting community. If youre from Fort Pierce, you know how we get down,' owner Darrion Henry said. How they get down at A Future Worth Fighting 4 was on full display at the 2026 Florida State Police Athletic League. WATCH: A local boxing gym brings the two C's: community and championships A local boxing gym brings the two C's: community and championships They finished with three state champions, a silver medalist, and a second-place overall team finish, and the star of the Tournament was none other than Justice Henry. He credits the gym's family-like atmosphere and tough-love environment for his success. This gym has been the biggest part of my life. Ive been boxing since I was eight years old, and this became a home for our own little community and us, with everyone we bring in here, said Henry. While Henry has been boxing since he was eight, he has a teammate, Frantzner Jean, whos just getting started but is already making a name for himself after winning his first fight by unanimous decision. It felt pretty fun; I just like the dopamine rush from it, said Jean. Every day after school, kids fill the gym to learn the sweet science of boxing, but there's one rule: you have to go to school every day. Im a teacher at Dan McCarty, so I can see how their behavior has changed, and now I have a lot of kids who show up to school because they know if they dont show up to school, Im going to get on them, said Henry. One of the kids taking the school-first approach is Michael Sanchez, whose dad signed him up for classes, but now hes ready to take this sport as far as it can go. I ended up liking it because I can learn from it, like discipline and hard work, said Sanchez.

entry.title: 'A huge loss’: Family remembers 24-year-old killed in Port St. Lucie hit-and-run - WPEC
entry.summary: 'A huge loss’: Family remembers 24-year-old killed in Port St. Lucie hit-and-run    WPEC
entry.article_text: A Port St. Lucie family is remembering their 24-year-old daughter after she was killed in a hit-and-run last week. Alexis Cuellar, known to her family as Lexi, was riding her scooter to work on Nov. 16 when she was struck by a vehicle near SW Gatlin Boulevard, according to police. She died the following day, Nov. 17. For the first time, her father and relatives are sharing memories of the young woman they say brought joy to everyone around her. Alexis wasn't just a ray of sunshine, you know. I think to us she was just the sun, her father, Alberto Vasquez, said As the eldest daughter, Vasquez said Alexis had a natural instinct to care for others, beginning with her own siblings. Ever since she was born she just, she had a passion for caring for others, starting with her siblings, you know, he said. At the family's Port St. Lucie home, Vasquez and relatives, some visiting from Texas, gathered around photos of Alexis as they remembered her life. She was the sweetest person ever, and it's a huge loss for the family, her aunt, Minerva Benitez, said. Also read: Port St. Lucie hit-and-run victim dies; driver could face more serious charges Vasquez said the support they have received has helped them. It's really helped us get through these first difficult days that were unbearable, he said. He remembered his daughter as someone who loved children and dreamed of working with them. He was also proud of her time in Junior ROTC. On the morning of the crash, Vasquez watched Alexis leave home for her job at Wendy's. She had been excited about picking up more hours. He said he saw her riding away on her scooter and assumed she would be OK. Five minutes later, he learned there had been a crash. Police have charged 18-year-old Tristian Ray Sanchez-Chasmer in connection with the crash. Investigators say he had been playing ding-dong-ditch with friends before getting behind the wheel of a Chevy Tahoe. He's accused of hitting Cuellar as she rode her scooter in a crosswalk, then leaving the scene. He is currently charged with leaving the scene. Additional charges, including vehicular homicide, could follow. Vasquez said he wishes he could have been there to help his daughter. I'm sorry that I couldn't be there for her, maybe help her. And that I loved her deeply because I didn't get a chance to tell her that, he said. Now, he is preparing a place at home where he plans to bring her. A service for Alexis will be held Wednesday, Nov. 25, at Haisley Funeral Home in Fort Pierce. Police are continuing to investigate the crash.

entry.article_text: A homeowner's quick call to 911 helped interrupt an attempted home invasion in Palm City early Tuesday, leading to the arrests of four people from Jacksonville, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office.The sheriff's office said the homeowner heard a noise outside a home on Southwest Bimini Circle in the Evergreen Club and contacted authorities. Investigators said at least one of the suspects was armed with a handgun.When deputies arrived, the four suspects scattered into the neighborhood, according to the sheriff's office. Deputies established a perimeter and, with assistance from the agency's aviation, drone and K-9 units and the Stuart Police Department K-9 unit, found all four hiding in separate locations throughout the community.Investigators believe the group parked near a canal and walked into the neighborhood to target the home. Deputies said they recovered a firearm, masks and gloves. Detectives later determined the gun had been reported stolen.The sheriff's office identified three of those arrested as 21-year-old Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr., 21-year-old Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews and 21-year-old Cameron Elijah Mapson. The fourth person arrested is 16 years old. WPTV is not naming the juvenile.All four face attempted home invasion charges and were taken into custody, according to the sheriff's office.Wise also faces charges of grand theft of a firearm and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.The sheriff's office credited the homeowner's quick decision to call authorities with interrupting the alleged crime before anyone was hurt.

entry.title: 4 men arrested after attempted home invasion at Martin County’s Evergreen Club - WPEC
entry.summary: 4 men arrested after attempted home invasion at Martin County’s Evergreen Club    WPEC
entry.article_text: A Palm City teenager's quick thinking may have stopped four men from breaking into his family's home at the Evergreen Club community off Murphy Road. The Martin County Sheriff's Office says the 17-year-old boy heard a noise outside their home on SW Bimini Circle at 3 a.m. Tuesday. He alerted his parents who called 911, interrupting the home invasion. When deputies arrived at the scene, the four suspects, three men and a teenager from Jacksonville, ran away in different directions. The sheriff's office says deputies set up a perimeter around the neighborhood with help from its aviation team, K-9 unit, and the Stuart Police Department. K9's were able to track down all four suspects hiding in separate locations throughout the community. The teen was found hiding in a bush outside the community. Two of the men were found hiding under a nearby bridge off Murphy Road. The fourth person was in a nearby parking lot who detectives believe was the getaway driver. The sheriff's office says at least one of the suspects was armed with a handgun. Sheriff John Budensiek said three of the four suspects have violent criminal histories. "These are bad, bad individuals who drove at least three and a half hours to Martin County to victimize a family that was going throughout their normal nightly routines," Budensiek said. Investigators said the suspects parked along the canal and walked half a mile into the neighborhood to target the home. The group is seen on home security video around 3 a.m. wearing dark clothing, masks and gloves. The sheriff said they tried to break in through a back door and covered a surveillance camera lens with a sticker. Deputies found masks, gloves and a firearm that had been stolen. Homeowners at the Evergreen Club community were shaken up. "I immediately woke up to Facebook and texts this morning, friends and family asked me if I was okay," said resident Katherine Willis. "Absolutely shocked that they would try to come in here. What are you going to get out of here? It's just very out of the ordinary for sure." The suspects were identified as: Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr, 22 Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews, 21 Cameron Elijah Mapson, 21 Teenage boy, 16 All four were charged with attempted home invasion. Wise faces an additional charge of grand theft and possession of a firearm. They're all being held in the Martin County Jail without bond. See also: Boca Raton police arrest man after reported assault on El Rio Trail The agency is asking Palm City residents to check their homes and vehicles for missing property or signs of a break-in. Anyone who finds anything missing should call the sheriff’s office at 772-220-7060. "The Martin County Sheriff's Office is heavily invested in protecting our community," Budensiek said. "To these traveling criminals, we're gonna put you away forever if we can."

entry.title: Aleksander Barkov, Brad Marchand activated, will return to Panthers lineup Wednesday against Senators
entry.summary: 'They're both in.' Those three words from Florida Panthers head coach Paul Maurice Wednesday morning could shift the balance of power in the NHL Atlantic Division and beyond. Panthers ready for Ottawa Senators and potential return of Barkov, Marchand Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand will both be in Wednesday's Panthers lineup against the Ottawa Senators at Amerant Bank Arena. After missing all of last season to a right knee injury, Barkov returned to the Panthers lineup this season only to injure his left knee in the second game. Marchand was injured the following game. Both have not played since their injuries. 'Pretty excited. Some of it's just the excitement of the unknown. We have no idea what well look like with both these guys in the lineup. Our core guys haven't played together since June of 25,' Maurice said. Maurice is referring to a timeframe when that core of Panthers, most of whom are still on the team, won the second straight Stanley Cup championship. 'It almost feels like the season starts tonight. Two guys will make you better over the long haul in a game like tonight,' Maurice said. Barkov is the Florida Panthers franchise all-time points leader. Marchand has scored 452 goals and played in 1,154 games in a Hall of Fame-worthy career to this point. The puck drop is set for 7 p.m. Wednesday. The game will air on WPTV and The Spot South Florida.

entry.article_text: Home Business News and Economic Updates in Sebastian, Florida Indian River County officials form Task Force 3 to help residents claim Amendment 3 property tax relief by Tina Hodges Nov 25, 2026 / 10:05 AM A A A A Reset Indian River County Tax Collector Carole Jean Jordan (left) and Property Appraiser Wesley Davis (right) Share on Twitter Share via Email VERO BEACH — Indian River County Tax Collector Carole Jean Jordan and Property Appraiser Wesley Davis announced Task Force 3, a joint initiative between their offices to help residents understand, qualify for, and receive the property tax benefits available under Florida’s newly approved Amendment 3. Voters approved Amendment 3 on Nov. 3. The measure makes significant changes to Florida’s property tax system beginning in 2027. Jordan and Davis said they are combining the resources, expertise, and public-service capabilities of their offices to help county residents navigate the changes. “We want to make sure every resident receives all the benefits they are entitled to receive,” the two officials said in announcing the initiative. Task Force 3 will focus on helping homeowners understand the new law, establish eligibility, satisfy residency requirements, obtain necessary documentation, and meet application deadlines. The effort will also assist real estate agents, title companies, attorneys, mortgage lenders, and others involved in property transactions by providing guidance intended to avoid costly delays or misunderstandings. “Carole Jean and I will spend the next six months talking to groups like the Board of Realtors, civic associations, homeowner associations, conducting media interviews, sponsoring town halls and speaking directly to individual residents, to make sure residents get what they voted for, said Davis. “We have established a technical committee of senior staff to collect, verify, and provide answers to the many questions people are asking,” Jordan added. entry.title: Heavy rain floods West Palm Beach roads, creates messy travel ahead of Thanksgiving
entry.summary: Heavy rain moved across the area Wednesday, flooding roads in parts of West Palm Beach. The soggy weather created a messy drive as people prepared to travel for Thanksgiving. Several areas of downtown West Palm Beach saw significant standing water as rain continued to fall. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Heavy rain, king tides cause flooding in downtown West Palm Beach At South Flagler Drive and Barcelona Road, water covered the roadway, forcing some drivers to turn around rather than attempt to make it through. WPTV reporter Christy Waite saw several cars turn around to avoid the area. Flooding was visible across several parts of the city. Near Ann Norton Sculpture Gardens, Palm Beach Atlantic University and the Palm Beach County Yacht Club, streets filled with water and even traffic cones could be seen floating in the roadway. Across from Elisabetta's Ristorante in downtown West Palm Beach, the water rose past Waite's boot as vehicles, including buses, continued navigating the flooded streets. From downtown, Waite traveled north to Lone Pine Estates in Riviera Beach , a neighborhood that has been hit especially hard by flooding this month. Neighbor Lacey Stone previously described how quickly conditions deteriorated. 'I have lived in Florida my whole life, and I have never seen anything like this; it just got worse and worse,' Stone said. The water in the neighborhood has since receded, but signs of the earlier flooding remain. Some residents still have sandbags outside their homes, while others continue dealing with damage left behind. Residents like Stephanie Gabriel never want to experience something like this again. 'This has been a devastating experience, and seeing all the damage it has caused is heart-wrenching,' Gabriel said. The flooding wasn't limited to the areas WPTV visited. As Waite headed back to the station, she found even more standing water, this time in WPTVs own parking lot in West Palm Beach.

entry.title: High water bill? Martin County says issue affecting 10 communities
entry.summary: A water meter data collection issue in Martin County caused some utility customers to receive unusually high water bills, according to Martin County Utilities. The county said the problem dates back about five months and affected the reporting of water usage for some customers. After the issue was corrected, water usage that had not previously been reported was reflected on a single month's bill, resulting in a higher-than-normal charge for affected customers. Martin County Utilities said the issue affects some customers in these communities: Legacy Cove Highlands Reserve Cove Isle Montego Cove Emerald Lakes Savannah Oaks Cove Lakes River Marina River Marina Estates Rocky Point Customers with questions about their bills or who need assistance can contact Martin County Utilities customer service at cservice@martin.fl.us. The county said a customer service representative can work with affected residents to establish a payment arrangement. Martin County Utilities said it has since implemented additional training and safeguards within its data collection software. Have you been affected? Let us know on our Facebook page!

entry.title: IRC sheriff renews push for unified 911 dispatch as Vero Beach weighs Amendment 3 cuts - WPEC
entry.summary: IRC sheriff renews push for unified 911 dispatch as Vero Beach weighs Amendment 3 cuts    WPEC
entry.article_text: Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers asked the Vero Beach City Council on Tuesday to take another look at merging emergency dispatch. He pitched it as a way to save money as the city prepares for revenue losses under Amendment 3 . Flowers said he first brought the idea to the council about two years ago. He said Brevard County has since moved to a unified dispatch system, and he told council members his offer still stands. "I'm not asking for anything specific today. I just want to make sure that it's known that it is my desire that we go to a unified dispatch system," Flowers said. He asked that it be considered "as a potential cost savings" as the city makes what he called "difficult decisions" under Amendment 3. Florida voters approved a ballot initiative that will slash non-school property taxes despite a campaign by local officials warning it would gut funding for public safety and other services. It will increase the homestead exemption from about $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Council member Tracey Zudans asked city staff to put numbers on the idea. "I'd love to see some numbers attached to it, not just response time numbers, but also some dollar numbers so that we can share that with our taxpayers as well," Zudans said. "I'd be happy to have my staff work with you guys," Flowers said. Mayor Aaron Vos said city staff will total what the city spends on dispatch now, and Flowers will bring back what it would cost the city to join a countywide call center. Vos said he expects a unified center would be run by the county, not the sheriff, similar to St. Lucie County's. Vice Mayor John Cotugno asked whether the dispatch center would be a county function or run by the sheriff's office. Flowers said the county technically runs dispatch, but most dispatchers work for his agency. "I have the bulk of dispatchers that work for me at the sheriff's office, so I can only offer it from my side," Flowers said. "You would have to ask the county if they were interested in maybe doing it differently." He added that the sheriff's office and the county are still discussing how Amendment 3 will affect their relationship. See also: 22-year-old West Palm Beach motorcyclist struck, killed by SUV in Loxahatchee That relationship has been strained before. In July 2025 a budget debate erupted during an Indian River County Commission meeting, prompting the board to call a 15-minute recess after tensions flared between commissioners and Flowers. Flowers was requesting $93.5 million that year, while the county recommended a budget closer to $83.5 million. Commissioners ultimately voted to raise the sheriff's budget by $6.8 million, far less than he requested. Flowers later sued the commission , which then held a special meeting over the sheriff's budget. "This is a very deep issue," Flowers said. "If we do it as a county, if we do it under me, either way, I'm just trying to get all of our dispatchers in the same room together." Council members took no action on the proposal. Vos said Amendment 3 means the city has to consider every option. "With the implications of Amendment 3, we have to look at all aspects of where we can save money," Vos said. "If it saves us money, that's what we need to do." But Vos said moving dispatch out of the police department could come with a hidden cost. "You could lose some of that rapport between the call center staff and the officers due to familiarity," he said. Vos said he talked with police leaders in Sebastian and Fellsmere after Flowers first pitched the idea. He said Sebastian police used the sheriff's call center until 2007, then went back to running their own. Vero Beach Police Chief David Currey said his position on keeping the city's dispatch center has not changed. Vero Beach and Sebastian police are the only agencies in the county that run their own dispatch. "The dispatchers know the officers. They know the community members," Currey said. "If we don't have that under our umbrella, then I don't have control over any of that." Currey said the department switched to a new computer-aided dispatch and records management system in June. He said the department is working with the sheriff's office to connect the two agencies' dispatch systems, which would let dispatchers see where deputies and officers are and handle calls without transferring them. Currey said the idea last came up around 2012. He said the sheriff at the time told the city that dispatching for Vero Beach would likely cost about the same, if not more. "We have ten dispatchers, and they have salaries, and they have benefits," Currey said. "That will cost him just like it'll cost us." Despite the uncertainty around Amendment 3, Currey said the department is not freezing hiring and is interviewing for a police officer position now.

"These are bad, bad individuals who drove at least three and a half hours to Martin County to victimize a family that was going throughout their normal nightly routines," Budensiek said. Investigators said the suspects parked along the canal and walked half a mile into the neighborhood to target the home. The group is seen on home security video around 3 a.m. wearing dark clothing, masks and gloves. The sheriff said they tried to break in through a back door and covered a surveillance camera lens with a sticker. Deputies found masks, gloves and a firearm that had been stolen. Homeowners at the Evergreen Club community were shaken up. "I immediately woke up to Facebook and texts this morning, friends and family asked me if I was okay," said resident Katherine Willis. "Absolutely shocked that they would try to come in here. What are you going to get out of here? It's just very out of the ordinary for sure." The suspects were identified as: Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr, 22 Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews, 21 Cameron Elijah Mapson, 21 Teenage boy, 16 All four were charged with attempted home invasion. Wise faces an additional charge of grand theft and possession of a firearm. They're all being held in the Martin County Jail without bond. See also: Boca Raton police arrest man after reported assault on El Rio Trail The agency is asking Palm City residents to check their homes and vehicles for missing property or signs of a break-in. Anyone who finds anything missing should call the sheriff’s office at 772-220-7060. "The Martin County Sheriff's Office is heavily invested in protecting our community," Budensiek said. "To these traveling criminals, we're gonna put you away forever if we can."

entry.title: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to nearly 4 years in $260K AI cryptocurrency fraud scheme
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie man has been sentenced to nearly four years in federal prison for using artificial intelligence to impersonate a popular online streamer as part of a cryptocurrency fraud scheme that authorities say cost victims about $260,000. David Anthony Sanchez, 36, was sentenced to 47 months in federal prison after pleading guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida. Federal prosecutors said Sanchez, who also went by 'Dave the Jewler,' 'Rueben Alexis De Jesus Santana' and other aliases, impersonated online streamer N3ON to convince organizers of a cryptocurrency memecoin project that the streamer had agreed to endorse and participate in it. According to court records, Sanchez created online accounts designed to look as though they belonged to N3ON and communicated with the project's organizers while posing as both the streamer and his representative. Prosecutors said Sanchez also executed agreements using N3ON's identity and sent organizers an AI-generated voice recording that mimicked the streamer's voice to falsely confirm his participation. Believing the representations were legitimate, the victims transferred approximately $260,000 in cryptocurrency to accounts controlled by Sanchez, according to prosecutors. Authorities said Sanchez later converted a substantial portion of the cryptocurrency into U.S. dollars through transactions designed to conceal the source and ownership of the money. Prosecutors said he used the proceeds for his personal benefit. 'Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm,' Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas said in the release. She said Sanchez exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate victims' trust and take their money. In addition to his 47-month prison sentence, Sanchez was ordered to pay restitution to the victims. The amount of restitution was not specified in the release. The FBI's Miami Field Office investigated the case.

entry.title: Aleksander Barkov, Brad Marchand activated, will return to Panthers lineup Wednesday against Senators
entry.summary: 'They're both in.' Those three words from Florida Panthers head coach Paul Maurice Wednesday morning could shift the balance of power in the NHL Atlantic Division and beyond. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Aleksander Barkov, Brad Marchand activated, will return to Panthers lineup Wednesday against Senators Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand will both be in Wednesday's Panthers lineup against the Ottawa Senators at Amerant Bank Arena. After missing all of last season to a right knee injury, Barkov returned to the Panthers lineup this season only to injure his left knee in the second game. Marchand was injured the following game. Neither has played since their injuries. 'Pretty excited. Some of it's just the excitement of the unknown. We have no idea what we'll look like with both these guys in the lineup. Our core guys haven't played together since June of 2025,' Maurice said. Maurice is referring to a timeframe when that core of Panthers, most of whom are still on the team, won the second straight Stanley Cup championship. 'It almost feels like the season starts tonight. Two guys will make you better over the long haul in a game like tonight,' Maurice said. Barkov is the Florida Panthers franchise all-time points leader. Marchand has scored 452 goals and played in 1,154 games in a Hall of Fame-worthy career to this point. The puck drop is set for 7 p.m. Wednesday. The game will air on WPTV and The Spot South Florida.

entry.title: What are king tides? These exceptionally high tides are increasingly flooding coastal communities
entry.summary: King tides are the highest tides of the year, and they are increasingly flooding coastal communities as sea levels rise. King tide is a non-scientific or colloquial term that people often use to describe these exceptionally high tides. The 2026 super El Nio the natural and temporary warming of parts of the Pacific has raised coastal water levels and intensified the effects of king tides. 'Tides are incredibly complicated. Really every location has different tidal cycles and that's the basis for what a king tide is,' said Alec Bogdanoff, an oceanographer and meteorologist in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. 'It's a local term for the highest high tides of the year in a location. And when it impacts you, that's when they call it a king tide.' Over a foot of rain floods southeast Florida; multiday threat looms King tides are happening more often King tides typically occur when the sun, moon and Earth are nearly aligned because their gravitational pull adds together. This raises water levels and produces the greatest tidal effects of the year. This can happen on both coasts around the same time because the tides are responding to the same alignment and proximity of the moon and sun. In 2026, El Nio caused higher baseline water levels on both coasts, Bogdanoff said. The highest high tides happen during full moons and new moons and seasonal cycles that can raise or lower sea levels, he added. Historically, many coastal areas saw king tides once or twice a year, but some places are experiencing them more often than that as sea levels rise. And when it impacts you, that's when they call it a king tide."King tides are happening more oftenKing tides typically occur when the sun, moon and Earth are nearly aligned because their gravitational pull adds together. This raises water levels and produces the greatest tidal effects of the year. This can happen on both coasts around the same time because the tides are responding to the same alignment and proximity of the moon and sun. In 2026, El Niño caused higher baseline water levels on both coasts, Bogdanoff said.The highest high tides happen during full moons and new moons and seasonal cycles that can raise or lower sea levels, he added.Historically, many coastal areas saw king tides once or twice a year, but some places are experiencing them more often than that as sea levels rise.King tides can cause floods in coastal communitiesBecause king tides bring unusually high water levels, they can cause local tidal flooding. Strong winds and storms can make that flooding worse.Bogdanoff said the stormwater systems don't function normally when ocean water is higher than the levels they were designed for.Climate change is raising risksClimate change is driving and accelerating sea level rise. Glaciers and ice sheets are melting and the sea's waters are expanding as they warm. As this happens, flooding from king tides is becoming more frequent and it's increasingly disrupting life along the coasts.Four California locations recorded their all-time highest observed water levels in late October, and near-record king tides flooded some low-lying communities there as Thanksgiving travel ramped up."El Niño is natural, the sea level rise we're seeing now isn't," Bogdanoff said. "The flooding we're seeing with these king tides is a preview of what's to come in the 2030s and beyond."In 2011, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said sea level rise will make current king tides become the future's everyday tides.Coastal areas prepare for king tidesBogdanoff said coastal communities can do stormwater assessments and adaptation plans that take into account future projections for sea level rise, like his home state is doing with its Resilient Florida Program. Bogdanoff is principal scientist and co-founder of Brizaga, an engineering and consulting firm that helps communities plan for flooding and sea level rise.Next steps could include raising roads, figuring out better ways to protect the coastlines, finding more green space that absorbs water and building bigger stormwater systems that rely more on pumps than gravity to drain the water quicker — projects that will take time, he added."In some communities it's a much bigger conversation about what the future looks like," he said. "We don't have to fix everything at once. We just need to make sure the next decision is a little smarter than the last one."

entry.title: 'A huge loss’: Family remembers 24-year-old killed in Port St. Lucie hit-and-run - WPEC
entry.summary: 'A huge loss’: Family remembers 24-year-old killed in Port St. Lucie hit-and-run    WPEC
entry.article_text: A Port St. Lucie family is remembering their 24-year-old daughter after she was killed in a hit-and-run last week. Alexis Cuellar, known to her family as Lexi, was riding her scooter to work on Nov. 16 when she was struck by a vehicle near SW Gatlin Boulevard, according to police. She died the following day, Nov. 17. For the first time, her father and relatives are sharing memories of the young woman they say brought joy to everyone around her. Alexis wasn't just a ray of sunshine, you know. I think to us she was just the sun, her father, Alberto Vasquez, said As the eldest daughter, Vasquez said Alexis had a natural instinct to care for others, beginning with her own siblings. Ever since she was born she just, she had a passion for caring for others, starting with her siblings, you know, he said. At the family's Port St. Lucie home, Vasquez and relatives, some visiting from Texas, gathered around photos of Alexis as they remembered her life. She was the sweetest person ever, and it's a huge loss for the family, her aunt, Minerva Benitez, said. Also read: Port St. Lucie hit-and-run victim dies; driver could face more serious charges Vasquez said the support they have received has helped them. It's really helped us get through these first difficult days that were unbearable, he said. He remembered his daughter as someone who loved children and dreamed of working with them. He was also proud of her time in Junior ROTC. On the morning of the crash, Vasquez watched Alexis leave home for her job at Wendy's. She had been excited about picking up more hours. He said he saw her riding away on her scooter and assumed she would be OK. Five minutes later, he learned there had been a crash. Police have charged 18-year-old Tristian Ray Sanchez-Chasmer in connection with the crash. Investigators say he had been playing ding-dong-ditch with friends before getting behind the wheel of a Chevy Tahoe. He's accused of hitting Cuellar as she rode her scooter in a crosswalk, then leaving the scene. He is currently charged with leaving the scene. Additional charges, including vehicular homicide, could follow. Vasquez said he wishes he could have been there to help his daughter. I'm sorry that I couldn't be there for her, maybe help her. And that I loved her deeply because I didn't get a chance to tell her that, he said. Now, he is preparing a place at home where he plans to bring her. A service for Alexis will be held Wednesday, Nov. 25, at Haisley Funeral Home in Fort Pierce. Police are continuing to investigate the crash.

entry.title: Neighbors plead for help as repeated flooding threatens their Indian River County homes - WFLX
entry.summary: Neighbors plead for help as repeated flooding threatens their Indian River County homes    WFLX
entry.article_text: People across South Florida and the Treasure Coast are bracing for yet another round of heavy rain , and one Indian River County community is pleading for help after battling repeated flooding this month. Joe Waters documented his frustration Saturday evening, recording on his phone in front of his mobile home in the Heritage Plantation mobile home park near Vero Beach as a car drove through floodwaters that almost covered its headlights. Waters said the wake caused by passing vehicles crashed into the bricks that protect the undercarriage of his home, toppling them. “The water came up probably about thigh high,” Waters said. “Came up into the driveway, went into the house.” Waters and his wife were able to clean their home, but he said his car is still in the shop with $4,600 worth of damage, waiting on approval from the insurance company. When we showed up at Heritage Plantation Tuesday afternoon, a crowd of neighbors gathered — fed up after battling multiple floods just this month. Dawn Carboni, the HOA president, told me she wants to be a voice for her neighbors, especially those who can’t speak up. “They just want to feel safe in their homes,” she said. The flooding has created dangerous conditions for emergency responders, Carboni said. “We had a gentleman who needed EMS to come out, and they could not get to his home, so they had to park out on 82nd (Avenue), and then a large fire truck had to get to the home,” Carboni said. With more heavy rain in the forecast, Carboni said residents are frightened. It’s horrible living in fear when you don’t know if it’s going to rain and you’re going to be able to leave your home the next day.” She wants to spread awareness about what her community is going through. “We need help, and we’re asking for help,” Carboni said. Emergency managers in Indian River County tell me they’re operating at a Level 2 emergency, meaning the Emergency Operations Center is partially activated. They’ve extended the state of emergency through Sunday, Nov. 30. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

entry.title: Heavy rain renews flood concerns as most Florida homeowners lack flood insurance
entry.summary: Another round of heavy rain in Florida is once again raising concerns about flooding and flood insurance. According to the Insurance Information Institute, as much as 80% of Florida homeowners don't carry flood insurance, even though just one inch of water in a home can cause $25,000 in damage. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Most Floridians Still Pass on Flood Insurance 'Everyone is in a flood zone,' says Lee Wiglesworth of Wiglesworth Rindom Insurance in Stuart. 'It's just a matter of if you're in a high risk or a low risk.' He said many pass on the coverage because of costs, being in a low-risk zone and also not fully understanding their homeowners policy. 'If a hurricane comes and creates a flooding event, they think I have hurricane coverage,' he said. But those claims are often denied since homeowners policies only cover wind damage. Experts say relying on FEMA in flood situations can leave homeowners short, since FEMA grants will cover temporary housing and essential repairs. National flood insurance will cover $250,000 on the structure and $100,000 on the contents of a home. Costs for flood insurance can vary from $600 to $1,300 a year. In addition to national flood insurance, there are also options for flood insurance with private insurers, and there are waiting periods before policies become active.
